What a great end to Selva Almada’s masculinity trilogy. This had such a Brickmakers feel to it with the dancing and the small town community feel. I felt slightly confused whilst reading it as it really breaks the boundaries between past and present, living and dead, as it seems to tell multiple stories at once and flicks back and forth to different timelines. But reading the translators note by Annie McDermott (who I adore) was really beneficial as it made a lot more sense how she wanted the prose to match not only the original rural Argentine text but to mirror the river-like quality of her original writing, as the story ebbs and flows between seemingly different versions of reality. The prose is very Carson McCullers and in this final instalment it is completely stripped back to its bare bones. There is no speech marks and the line and paragraph breaks transform the text into something akin to poetry. I feel it is the most experimental of her works but also the most lyrical and surreal. Its length worked well with the subject matter and structure. Whilst Brickmakers will always be my favourite Almada text I’m glad this one had remnants of it to carry me through. Really excited to see what she will explore next now that she has put her seal on such a varying and brutal representation of Latin American masculinity.

Charco only publishes bangers and Not A River is no exception. A short little thing at less than 100 pages and written sparsely at that. It’s the very definition of bare bones and seeing McDermott credit Cormac McCarthy as an influence in her translation makes perfect sense. Boundaries are blurred between time and place, between the living and the dead, but done so effectively that a choice word, a slight suggestion dropped is enough to orient the reader. There’s no confusion, just admiration at the swift and subtle shifts linking the corporeal world with the spiritual. Though most boundaries are fuzzy, hard lines are drawn between the two groups at the center of this masculine story. It’s an us vs. them from the start with the islanders and outsiders and one can sense the mounting violence that will surely erupt by the book’s end. Enjoyed & recommend. A welcome addition to the IB longlist!

"This man isn’t from these woods and the woods are well aware. But they leave him be. He can come in, he can stay for as long as it takes to gather kindling. Then the woods themselves will spit him out, his arms full of branches, back to the shore." Not A River (written by Selva Almada and translated from Spanish by Annie McDermott) opens with three men (Enero and El Negro who are in their 50s, and Tilo, the son of their late friend Eusebio), who were out on a fishing trip on an Island in the Parana. They caught a huge sting ray by shooting it and thereafter hung it on a tree. Several islanders (Aguirre being their ring-leader) noticed the sting ray but when Enero threw the sting ray back into the river, Aguirre and his gang were enraged. There are several flashbacks throughout the story (in a deliberate fragmentary prose) where we learn more about Eusebio's death, the past of Aguirre's sister, Siomara, and the death of Siomara's daughters (Mariela and Lucy, who invited Tilo to a dance in the form of ghosts). Almada is a master at creating tensions between characters as well as the violence that was inflicted on the characters. Through atmospheric descriptions, we feel the rage, the "unwelcome" attitude, and the prejudice that arouse amongst the islanders against the outsiders (Enero, El Negro, and Tilo). The river, the deaths, and tragedies, the ghosts of the past, the forest, the nightclubs, all represent toxic masculinity, loss, grief, and resilience, especially in a small-town setting. As explained in the translator's notes, "the line breaks and lack of chapter divisions make the text itself river-shaped, its short sentences lapping at the silence like waves on the shore". Not A River is definitely a short, yet powerful piece of work. A strong 4/5 star read and a worthy shortlist for the 2024 International Booker Prize.

Let me start by saying that I have never read any social horror as good as the ones written by Latin American women. This is my third Selva Almada, and now she is firmly on my list of favourite authors. In Not A River by Selva Almada (translated by Annie McDermott), two close friends go camping to a remote island with the son of a friend who had died in a terrible accident. As they encounter their pasts and the local islanders, things get much darker. This is a book that lingers, seeps into your skin. There is a feeling of grief unresolved, tragedy unfolding again. At the same time, a sense of foreboding and an inexplicable sense of terror. Things feel dreamlike and realistic. The people in it like phantoms, but also uncomfortably real. A ghost story in some ways - the ghost of memories, ghosts of things lost, and the ghosts that seem more alive than the living. Like Almada's previous novels, Not A River is an exploration of the toxicity of hyper-masculinity. The casual, violent misogyny; the dismissive attitude towards the female characters; the uncomfortable objectification; the women in the book like silhouettes rather than humans. Yet, these very men also seem stripped open in their pathetic weaknesses and the nightmares that taunt them at night. In just under 100 pages, Almada conveys so much complexity, imparted through an elegant, melancholic writing.

My second book of International Booker longlist 2024. Honestly, even though it was very suggestive, tense and atmospheric I was quite bored with it. It reminded me of those kinds of novels you're assigned in school to work out themes and motifs and that everybody slogs through and don't like. Like I'm sure it's very good from a critical standpoint it wasn't very enjoyable to me.
I finished the book confused about the story (maybe mesmerized is a better word), but 100% convinced this was some great piece of writing. 4.5
Masterful. This is one of our best living writers.

Not a River (⭐3.5/5) by Selva Almada Almada's short novel is anything but straightforward. It glides between past and present with ease and makes you lose yourself in its flow. but unlike a river, it doesn't flow in one direction. It takes the point of view of various characters while focusing on their past traumas and corresponding emotional ghosts that still live with them. Like many other similar spanish (and Japanese) work, I feel like some of it gets lost in translation. The expression of very complex emotions somehow gets subdued because of which, some characters appear unnaturally mechanical. Still, the book does an amazing job describing how past traumas and mistakes have the power to haunt not only people but also a place that saw it and how because of this, it becomes bound to repeat the cycle of darkness again and again.

Well, this was an excellent read, a book that truly gets under your skin. The title says Not a River but that is exactly what this feels like, it is gentle, slowly meandering along making you feel relaxed and comfy, there are the odd warning signs that something is going on here and before you know it the river has spun you around and has claimed another reader. The writing is unusual, the dialogue has been stripped down to just the odd words between characters, no long speeches here, everything else has also been stripped right back too, each scene and lack of chapter borders makes this feel like one piece of prose…it is really rather refreshing, you don’t realise you need a book like this until you have finished it. There were odd moments in the story that had me scratching my head, the warning signs I mentioned before, little things like a throwaway phrase “smooth sheets” did I just read that right? Was it an error in translation? Head is scratched and reader moves on…then boom! one short line and all those “errors” come together and it was so shocking, rest of the book was read in awe. Charco press are forever putting out amazing translations and this book was so unique that Annie McDermott had to include a small afterword to explain her process on translating a book like this. Do not skip this just cos you have finished the story, she explains her technique and it is so very important the extra steps she takes to get the translation perfected, something A.I. can never do. Massive thanks to McDermott for the extra work she put in because without that this reader never would have had the chance to read this…let alone enjoy it as much as I did. I... I don't have the words. I'll try to write a review but bear with me. First, let me just say that if anything happens to Ruhn and Hunt I am going to riot. And yes, that's a threat. Ok, now to the review. This book stressed me. I can't even count the number of times I had to put it down and walk away for a minute because I was scared to read what happened next. I loved the dynamic and I loved how Ruhn's house just kept getting more and more crowded and they all just accepted it like it was nothing. That brood of highly competent, badass idiots are all my babies and they better come out unscathed. Then there was Bryce and Hunt. I love them. The banter, the chemistry, loyalty, and love they have between them is everything. Nothing will ever come close. I was worried about Hunt, I'm not gonna lie. Sarah has a tendency to bait us into falling for one guy, just for another dude to come in for the win. But no, Bryce and Hunt were everything together. There's nothing else to say. Overall, this was great. I loved it. Not as much as I did the first book, I have to admit. But I loved it. And no, this wasn't really a review. I didn't even mention the plot of the novel, but if you've made it this far you probably already know what it's about. I just needed to gush about these characters for a bit since no one in real life will get excited and talk about these characters with me. So yeah. That is all. Go read this book. Talk about it with me in the comments. That ending left me with too many emotions. Goodbye. But before you go! My final question to this all, the one that has bothered me since book one and plagues me to this day: how does a faun dance ballet? Like actually though? You can't be on pointe with hooves and bent legs. Every time they mentioned June dancing my brain almost spontaneously combusted trying to conjure up a visual! At this point, I just assume that Juniper is to ballet, what Feyre is to painting and I'll leave it at that!

Final reread before CC3: January 16 2024 New rating 3.5/5 In my previous review I mentioned that I would most likely never pick up CC 2 again...and boy am I happy that I did. Reading this novel knowing what happens at the end, the spoilers, who everyone really is...is a completely different experience. My mistake when I first read CC2 was that I had completely forgotten what happened in the first instalment. Now, in 2024, I read CC2 right after CC 1 and wow...I understand everything so much better. All together, I had a much better reading experience the second time around and I am so happy that I gave this book a proper shot. Yes, some things in my previous review are still correct. The plot was not solidified well, there was alot of filler information and people, the POVs were confusing, and it felt very male centered....however, I cannot deny that craft and thought behind the entirety of the novel. SJM is just too damn good. Even though the middle still dragged on like crazy, reading it while knowing the ending had me reading between the lines. I did not expect to enjoy it so much. maybe it was the excitement of CC3 coming out in two weeks, but I truly appreciate the work and time this must have taken to write. I feel bad that i despised my first read so much, I despise that I began to skim throughout and missed out on the full experience of the novel. At the end of the day, SJM is just so intentional. I love how she brings everything full circle. She is one of the best fantasy writers in this generation. she can make me cry so easily. I really loved this, there were slow and confusing parts if we want to be detailed, but after reading the ending again...wow I have chills. I am so excited to see what she has planned after a decade! If you did not enjoy your first time reading, I HIGHLY recommend giving it a reread right after the first instalment. ------------------------------- 3/5- February 2022 Honestly, I waited for this book for so long and am slightly conflicted with how I feel about this story as a whole. I have never rated a SJM novel this low before. I was sometimes forcing myself to read it - like it was some university homework . But I also liked how she took this series to an entire new level- I can tell there was a lot of research done. Pros: 1. Ruhn and his love story. That storyline between day and night was the most surprising and delightful thing out of this book. The way these two have a hold on me right now. That ending elevator scene was one of the best in the book!! I was here for it!!! 2. The secondary characters and the otters awwwww 3. THE ENDING- what else can I say about that!! Cons: 1. The plot was just not there for me. I could not feel any major stakes for the characters throughout. They were all fighting a fight that they all barely seemed to even want to be apart of. The majority of the novel was just everyone talking all the time and info dumping loads and loads of things. I genuinely got a headache reading it- like my head still hurts. And also not to mention, the amount of new characters being added. Everyone is so powerful, everyone has this power and blah blah blah- like no one felt special at all because there was every kind of type of being. It’s like SJM took every mythical creature to exist and dump them in 800 pages. 2. The POVS were too much. Honestly I love a good multiple POV novel but this was just over doing it. Tell me why there was POV switches mid chapter- and sometimes even three switches. It was honestly too much and the characters really all started to blend into each-other sadly. No one stood out to me, even Bryce. I also was noticing the lack of female POVS. At some points it was all just Bryce in the room of men. Once I caught on, I couldn’t stop pointing it out. This novel felt very male centred and I was so over it by the end. 3. The main romance was unnatural and boring . I’m sorry but this book made Bryce and Hunt so boring. For a novel that promises lots of heat and tension…. It was barely there honestly. It was at no point a ACOMAF type of romance for me (but nothing will ever be). I also got annoyed with how many times Bryce said alphahole and ashole like girl… we’re all over it. Almost everyone of her remarks back had to have some vulgar swearing in it. It was fun first but it gets tired very quickly. My final thoughts for this is that I truly think this novel by itself, was a complete filler for the next one. SJM honestly did not need to write 800 pages of this boring confusing stuff. She could have just given us 200 pages and that last chapter TBH. I see what she did and it was in a way very smart because THE LAST CHAPTER HAD ME SHAKING OKAY! I have hope in the next one because there is an amazing foundation to work with. But for me, I will likely not pick up House of Sky and Breath again.

Bryce is trying to adapt to her new reality as the Princess of Fae, while also trying to work things out with Hunt to build a healthy and serious relationship. Hunt is enjoying his newfound freedom and Ruhn is building back the trust between his sister and him. "You'd almost think this was planned by the gods. They probably have a special task force: How to Fuck Over Bryce and Hunt in One Day." The plot is good, but I didn’t find it as good as in the first book. It is full of unexpected twists and shocking revelations though, and the pace is engaging. My heart was pounding and I had to refrain from skimming parts of the book because I was so anxious to know what would happen, but at the same time, I wanted to take my time and savor this book... Conflicted emotions and a few heart attacks apart though, it is a great book and many details from the first book have a big significance in this book, and I like that there was a deeper connection between the books than simply having the same set of characters embarking on a new adventure. "Our insurance rates will go sky-high," Ruhn said to Declan, appealing to the slightly-less-insane of his roommates. "When the fuck did you become a grown-up?" Flynn barked. Ithan jerked his own chin toward the doorway again. "Wait to have your meltdown until after you meet the fourth new roommate." “I’m sorry,” Ithan said, scrubbing at his face, “but what the fuck is this about?” He glanced at the pizza on the table, as if wondering whether it had been spiked with something. Welcome to our lives, Hunt wanted to say. "You're part of the Quinlan-Silago clan now. We're a crazy bunch, but we love each other." I LOVE the characters in this book, THEY ARE SO CUTE AND PERFECT TOGETHER. SJM worked her magic once again and made me fall in love with them as I did fall in love with the crew of ACOTAR and TOG. The secondary characters are as lovable and amazing as the main characters. The friendship developing between the guys in this book is so cute and wholesome! Ruhn, Flynn, Declan, Tharion, Hunt, and even Ithan are becoming a cute little boy's club and my heart is SO happy about that. I said in my review of the first book that I wanted more of Ithan and Tharion, and I got it! Hypaxia is also more present in this book and I can already see that Bryce and her will make a kickass duo. Okay, now this might be an unpopular opinion, but in light of what we learned in this book, I was not impressed with Danika’s choices and behavior toward Bryce, and the friendship I admired so much in the first book turned a little sour. I feel that Bryce gave her everything to Danika, and Danika only gave her a few pieces. I know Danika loved Bryce fiercely, but she kept so many huge secrets from Bryce, and every time Bruce discovers a new truth about Danika, it only upsets her because she sees how little she truly knew about her best friend… She said to Flynn, “Hey, remember that time you set a dragon free and were dumb enough to think she’d follow your orders?” “Hey, remember that time you wanted to marry me and wrote Lady Bryce Flynn in all your notebooks?” Hunt choked. Bryce countered with, “Hey, remember when you pestered me for years to hook up with you, but I have something called standards—” “This is highly unusual behavior for royals,” Hypaxia observed. The found family is one of my favorite tropes, and I loved every mundane moment with the gang in this book because of this feeling of finally having somewhere to belong. From Hunt making new friends to Ithan and Rhun mending their relationship with Bryce, it was cute, sweet, and so satisfying to see them all finally feel like they belonged somewhere and had people who cared about them. She sipped from her champagne, then said casually to Hunt, "The headline on the gossip sites tomorrow is going to be: Horndog Umbra Mortis gropes Starborn Princess at Ballet." "Good," Hunt murmured. "It'll improve my standing in the 33rd." "You know what I mean," Bryce said. "I'm not sure I do." Had his voice dropped lower? "We're roomies," she said, her own voice getting breathy. "Roomies." "Occasional Beer Pong Champion?" Hunt snatched the hat off her head and plunked it back on his own, backward as usual, "Yes, the Autumn King truly fears our unholy beer pong alliance." The romance between Bryce and Hunt is still super cute, and we also have more spicy moments, even though SJM did ensure that Hunt got cockblocked quite a few times before *it* finally happened. They are cute and funny and they still have that witty banter from the first book that I enjoyed so much. I like that the author managed to keep the sexual tension between them for so long and that when they finally did the deed, they didn’t turn into sex-obsessed fae/angel and did nothing else for the rest of the book. They enjoyed each other but kept in mind that they had more important things to do and that there were lives on the line. “Hel’s armies shall strike at your command, Bryce Quinlan.” I am a little disappointed though that Aidas was not more present in this book. I really like him, and I think he has the potential to be a truly complex and interesting morally grey character, but we haven't seen enough of him to really know what he is up to and where he stands in the conflict that is to come. I can't wait for the next book. There is SO MUCH potential for an even more epic third book, but at the same time, I am SO FREAKING SCARED of what could happen to my babies. 😭😭😭😭😭 Hunt’s voice was a thunderclap as he said behind her, “Light it up, Bryce.” 1. Well, friends. That’s it. Crescent City 2: House of Sky and Breath will be the last Sarah J. Maas book I will ever read. What a disaster. What exactly is the plot of this 800-page nightmare? And with a super perfect, overpowered, every-dude-wants-to-bang-her main character, this just feels like another weird vanity project so SJM can live in a fantasy world where everyone loves her and her husband can never leave her. I just…what did I just read? PLOT SUMMARY: After saving Crescent City, Bryce and Hunt just want to lay low. But they can’t. SUBPLOT SUMMARIES: WHICH INCLUDES SPOILERS. HEADS UP FOR THE PEOPLE ON GR’S APP! -The gang searches for a human Thunderbird (whatever that is) and her brother, but (view spoiler) -Ruhn becomes an inept spy and (view spoiler) -Ithan moves in and moves out, is concerned about his brother’s soul, and then (view spoiler) -Bryce is forced by her father to get engaged to Cormac, her asshole cousin who (view spoiler) -Bryce bickers with her only female friends. -Tharion doesn’t want to get married so he (view spoiler) -Despite being the most powerful person ever at the end of CC1, Bryce discovers she’s (view spoiler) -Danika is inexplicably still a major part of this story and somehow has even more secrets, (view spoiler) -Humans continue to be put into concentration camps and our main characters (view spoiler) -Bryce and Hunt are (view spoiler) You might be thinking, “Wow, that’s a lot you just listed, and yet you’re still saying, there’s no plot?” That’s correct, my friends. All of those subplots (and I didn’t even list them all) just circle around each other like giant turds in a toilet bowl. The storylines either stop abruptly or never have a payoff. This is really disappointing because even though I didn’t like the first book, there were some plot points that I was interested in seeing how they would play out. I was most interested in how Aidas and Jesiba were going to factor into the plot. (view spoiler) This book doesn’t accomplish anything in terms of character development and seems like a 790 page buildup for a cliffhanger ending. And I’m sure most Maas fans will love that ending, and I get it. But from the standpoint of good writing, it’s severely lacking. (view spoiler) I am just completely confused on why SJM set up this world where humans are being put into concentration camps, and yet Bryce, who is half human, doesn’t really do anything to help her own people. Because she’s able to pass as Fae, this injustice does not seem to concern her in the slightest. I would be fine if the book acted like it was aware of the main character having what is essentially White Privilege within this fantasy world, but there is a total disconnect between the injustice that is happening to an entire species of people in this book and the wacky hijinks our characters get up to. Instead of actually doing something to help others, they act completely self-righteous while the human rebels are portrayed as being the absolute worst. I just don’t get this at all. I don’t get why SJM decided to make human slavery and genocide the backdrop for the book while moving a public gym sex scene and so many references to Bryce’s thong underwear to the forefront. Seriously??? Having said all of that, this is my goodbye to Sarah J. Maas. I enjoyed ACOTAR when it was just me reading it and not having to listen to an entire fandom bow down before her and worship her every writing flaw. I’m just at a point where I feel like she is creatively bankrupt and shows no signs of making her books stronger or more interesting. And honestly, maybe she shouldn’t. If her fandom is happy with reading yet another story where the female protagonist has every single male character drooling over her while she ignores the basic rights of an entire species, then I guess I can see why she feels justified in not changing a damn thing. I wish her all the best, but this is it for me. I’m tucking and rolling off the SJM train. Y’all have fun without me.

⬆️Opening: This book was rough. I normally love Sarah J. Mass’s works but I haven’t been this disappointed by anything she’s written since A Court of Frost and Starlight. A lot of characters motives were weak, nothing of note happened in the first half, the MMC and FMC barely developed at all, the romance and spice lacked any semblance of chemistry, the pacing was way too slow, the plot wasn’t epic enough up until the very end, the two main characters were too strong with no justifiable cause and plot lines and characters that were hinted at being more prominent in this book never came to fruition. I loved Bryce in House of Earth and Blood, but in House of Sky and Breath her extreme “specialness” and ability to come out on top of every single situation just made her really annoying and bland to me. The only real improvement this book made was highlighting Ruhn, Ithan and the Hind more as a characters. 🔀Plot & Pacing: In terms of stakes, somehow the author managed to funnel out any and all tension and excitement this book should have had, in lue of meandering meaningless content. When I say absolutely nothing of importance happened in the first half of this book, I mean it. 300-400 pages of squat shit that did fuck all to advance the plot or develop a single character in any way. The book may be 800 pages long, but I feel like I only got 350 pages worth of content. This is supposed to be epic fantasy, but really nothing about this story was epic anyhow, besides the ending. I let the first book get away with 600+ pages of preamble before the finale because it was the first book in the series. It takes time to build towards epic stakes, especially in fantasy. However, the end of book one had a lot of momentum to help the plot of book two propel forward at a much better pace. Not that it meant anything though apparently, because this book doesn’t use any of the momentum that started in House of Earth and Blood. Instead, House of Sky and Breath just puts you back at square one to go through all the same boring preamble from HOEAB all over again, but without any character development, world-building or satisfying plot twists to distract from the sluggish pacing. 🐉World-Building: The first book had a slew of info-dump world-building. The second book counteracts this by hardly world-building at all. Seriously, for a series that’s supposedly about this amazing huge intricate magic city, the author really doesn’t show or tell you much about it… at all. The series is called Crescent City and yet that same city could be destroyed in the next book and I would just think “oh well”. Where are the adventures to magic hotels with an obscenely impossible amount of rooms, or a night club run by sirens that entrances its guests? Where are the murder mysteries at masquerade balls thrown by fae nobles? Where are the fascinating and scary and beautiful things this otherworldly magic city has to offer? Because as far as I can tell, besides being inhabited by magical beings, it’s just a normal modern human city for the most part and absolutely nothing about it is particularly interesting or magical. ❤️Romance: The biggest thing holding this book back is the obscene amount of time spent on Hunt and his romance with Bryce, and how it’s all about as interesting and believable as a glowing turd. Which leads me to my next point: Hunt and Bryce have all the chemistry of two crumbled up pieces of paper that just so happened to end up in the same garbage bin. Seriously, there was so little chemistry and tension between them that I actually skimmed their spicy scenes together. I never skim spicy scenes. The romance has to be truly awful to make me that uninterested in literal porn. It was so bad that when they started “confessing their love” for each other, I would just start laughing. Their romance was so implausible that their lovey dovey moments were just cringe. Once they started calling each other mates I had to skip a few sentences here and there, because even Bryce and Hunt themselves canonically aren’t even sure if they are mates. So their entire mating bond was very wishy-washy. And I usually love the romance in SJM novels, but this is arguably her worst romance yet. Am I probably being dramatic? Yes. Does that mean I think it’s not as bad as I’m making it out to be? No. The Brycehunt romance is truly quite horrendous. At this point the best I can hope for is that they aren’t endgame. Seriously, nothing could salvage this ship (for me at least). 💨Male Main Character: Hunt is, well about as complex as you can image. Which is to say not at all. I feel like I’m continually being told Hunt and Bryce are in love, instead of being shown they are in love. Also, I feel like basically all of Hunt’s “feats of bad-assery” (for lack of better words) are based solely in his reputation. I don’t feel like I’ve ever actually seen the Umbra Mortis live up to his name, at all. So when characters gawp and scatter, I don’t care, because he’s not scary or badass to me (the reader). I’m also getting really fucking sick of everyone getting called out on their shitty behaviour towards Bryce, except for Hunt. The book won’t ever let the reader forget that Ithan, Fury, Ruhn, etc cut off Bryce and the story is constantly reminding you of that and insisting they have to be better. Meanwhile, Hunt lied and manipulated Bryce all while living in her home and got to be magically forgiven for that by everyone. Including Ithan, Ruhn, Juniper, and Fury, who have absolutely no reason to forgive him based on who they are as characters. Honestly, Hunt never once getting called out when everyone else does, is starting to look like a major plot hole. I’m sorry, but cutting off a friend for a couple years is nowhere near as bad as lying to your romantic partner about the death of their best friend, knowingly possessing vital information that connects to them personally as you insert yourself into their life and then use them to accomplish a secret personal goal. Of all people, why is Hunt the only one that is instantly forgiven by every single character for seemingly no reason? Including Bryce, who forgave Hunt after only what, three days??? When prior to that she felt so wronged she never wanted to see him again?? The author likes to act like Bryce possessing personal information she didn’t immediately disclose to Hunt is just as bad as all the shit he did to her (which it isn’t). And as it turns out she was right not to reveal all her secrets to this random stranger, since he ultimately did use almost all the information she disclosed to him against her. Yet somehow he’s not the bad guy?? That’s a plot-hole. And if you’re wondering why I’m talking about Hunt’s characterization in book one instead of two, it’s because he didn’t develop or change at all in HOSAB. No, he didn’t apologize or redeem himself on any level. So there’s really nothing to say about him as a character in book two. He’s exactly the same. 🌟Female Main Character: Speaking of plot holes, Bryce is starting to seem too much like a super special chosen one in too many ways. In Throne of Glass the protagonist Aelin was raised as an assassin to infiltrate various organizations. So it made sense that she knew so much about fighting, politics, etc. In A Court of Thorns and Roses the protagonist Feyre had very little knowledge of how to do anything in relation to tactics or traditional education. She couldn’t even read; and thus it made sense that she was not really sure how to go about navigating the courts of Prythian. However, in Crescent City Bryce is a party girl in her mid-twenties, that has knowledge of how to use firearms, and that should be it based on how she’s written and who she’s presented to be as a character. But for whatever reason, she also knows how to wield a sword, is some kind of strategist that has knowledge of things that ancient politicians and royals don’t (for no reason) and is for whatever reason also capable of outsmarting individuals she should have no way of getting a leg up on. She isn’t frightened by things that frighten everyone else (on whatever grounds). Also, it’s never justified, but Ruhn wants Bryce to be queen of the fae despite the fact she’s never displayed any kind of suitable leadership skills and she actually lacks a lot of empathy for the fae people as a whole. So why does he want her to be queen? Because she’s the main character, that’s why. No other rationale is provided. She’s also liked by basically everyone. Yes, she has enemies, but that’s only because they stand on opposite sides of a conflict. As a whole, no one actually dislikes Bryce Quinlan. She’s just too fucking special. On top of that, she possesses the horn (a magical super weapon), received an incredible amount of power when she dropped into her immortality, is not only Starborn but a way more powerful Starborn than her brother, and can also teleport when lore-wise Ruhn should be able to do the exact same (but can’t/won’t for some reason that is never revealed). Bryce is also the rightful heir to her royal family (again, surpassing her brother for incredibly convient reasons that aren’t elaborated on) and is also this gorgeous witty woman that has no real flaws. The book also often goes out of its way (even so far as to create plot-holes) just to make Bryce look good. Bryce is a super-star in almost every regard, and she’s constantly becoming even more powerful and special, but never receives believable flaws or weaknesses to counteract all these strengths. In fact, the books try to convince you that Ruhn is the special chosen one and Bryce is the underdog, while simultaneously feeding the reader information that indicates the exact opposite. In the first book, Bryce was traumatized and grieving, and hadn’t become the perfect chosen one yet. Which made her quite compelling. In this book though, her biggest problem is becoming a princess, and that’s it. Her character became stagnant and too perfect as soon as House of Sky and Breath began. She barely develops as a character in this book at all, and as a result all of her “witty one-liners” and “burns” feel like hollow meaningless responses, instead of any real indication of wit. Bryce Quinlan is basically just a dollar store discount version of Aelin Galathynius at this point. 🚻Other Characters: It feels like Sarah J. Maas goes out of her way to try and make Bryce and Hunt as special as possible, and intentionally hinders other characters to achieve this, but by doing so she makes her secondary characters more compelling. By painting Bryce and Hunt as these super special, powerful, beautiful, perfect chosen ones, she ends up depicting characters like Ithan and Tharion as underdogs, which backfires and makes them more interesting than the actual main characters. There’s a reason why 80% of everything I’ve heard about HOSAB since it came out is about Ruhn and the Hind instead of Bryce and Hunt. And it’s because in the author’s quest to make Bryce and Hunt the chosen ones, she forgot to make them people. Their behaviour is never criticized or analyzed objectively. Everything they do is seen as acceptable at worst and god-like at best; painting them out to be too perfect to be real because they just magically know what to do (especially Bryce) even when they shouldn’t. Which is a big part of why them falling in love feels so hollow and lacklustre. As a whole, the best characters in the book were almost everyone except for the two that got the most page time. 📝Writing: The writing was pretty disappointing all things considered. For the majority of the book nothing really happens. Bryce and Co. meet up at her apartment, discuss a missing child, go off with the intention to do something, do nothing, come back to her apartment to discuss shit, rinse and repeat like six times for the next 500+ pages. Usually with high/epic fantasy you feel like the plot is building towards something important in a big way, but this book did not make me feel that. In fact, the first half of this book could be cut completely and the plot would have barely changed. In fact “the main plot” is actually revealed to be nothing of value once you’re about 500 pages deep into the book. After that, the characters decide to undertake a super risky endeavour for no truly viable reason. Almost everyone’s motives for risking their lives are very flimsy and don’t make much sense at all, and the fact that they go about it so carelessly and stupidly takes you out of the story. Again, it feels like the author is forcing characters to comply with what Bryce wants, not because it makes any sense, but because Bryce is the main character and thus everyone and everything should revolve around her. ⬇️Conclusion: As a whole, I do think Sarah J. Mass’s “golden age” of writing has come to pass. Her best works in my mind, are Throne of Glass books #3.0-#5.0 and A Court of Thorns and Roses book #1.0 and #2.0. Since then the quality of entertainment I’ve received from reading her novels has gradually declined. This review probably seems really bitter, but that’s new for me. I normally enjoy her work, but this book really pushed my buttons in terms of how much bullshit I can tolerate. I very much wish I had enjoyed this more. I wholly believe that if Bryce’s and Hunt’s characterization had been better and the pacing was faster, I would have appreciated this book a lot more. There were just far too many moments of weak writing and flimsy characterization for House of Sky and Breath to feel like anything but unsatisfactory to me.
I will never be okay again....

"To destroy monsters, we become monsters." Spice: 🌶️🌶️ I had no doubts whatsoever that this would be perfection. I love the sort of books that have me in a chokehold from page one and do not let go until they're over. I was so engrossed, I didn't stop reading until my eyes dried. It's just one shocking moment after the other until there's no brain left in your head. Also, I should have been used to Sarah J Maas's signature cliffhangers by now, but no. They still hurt and somehow amaze me at the same time. I feel like I survived a plane crash. Sure, I'm alive...but at what cost? Moreover, the love I feel for Bryce and Hunt has reached the highest of levels. Bryce is a beautiful cinnamon roll that could brutally kill you and has mean scheming skills (Rhysand and Aelin would be proud). Hunt is the softest killing machine and I would gladly lay down my life for him. I can see so much of Sarah's other characters in both of them and I love those parallels. Also, trying to figure out which of the winged bois has the biggest wingspan takes way too much of my time (I'm torn between Hunt and Azriel). What's more, I have never been more convinced that Bryce and Hunt are endgame. That sex scene alone should be enough to quell all our worries. If that doesn't do it for you, then the ending should be your biggest proof. There is no way he's pulling a Tamlin in the situation he is in at the moment. That's some mate-style angst right there. I know some people are coming up with these crazy anti-Bryce x Hunt theories and I am here to say that I completely and disrespectfully disagree! They are a perfect team, a beautiful couple, and they will overthrow their government with the power of their love! (OMG that was so cheesy 🤣) Furthermore, I really love Ruhn's storyline in this book. He has his own love story developing with the most unlikeliest of characters in the series, and a lot of angst to go with it. Said unlikely character has a pretty fascinating storyline too, and I can't wait to read more on that. I hope they mate in the next book. Unless Sarah decides to write their own book. (Doubtful, but a girl can hope.) Ruhn's character development is equally as fascinating. He becomes so much more than just the Rebel Prince going against his father's plans for him and it makes him all the more attractive. Additionally, Tharion needs to get his shit together ASAP. He makes some incredibly questionable decisions in this book and I wonder at his thought process. He went from sexy, mer-badass, to Princess "I wanna be where the people are" Ariel from one moment to the next. I love him, but he's a hot mess. Also, Ithan is the more sensible of the sexy bois in this book. He is basically everyone's white knight, although it took some time for him to come around. I feel bad for him too. He has this crush on Bryce and she has never even thought of him like that. He not only had to watch her flirt with his late brother incessantly, but now he has to watch her (or listen to her, more like) be all in love and horny for Hunt the Sexy Malakim. I hope he finds someone too. Lastly, even though Danika has been dead for 95% of this series, she is still a complete mystery. You would think Bryce was in on her secrets, but apparently that isn't. It isn't surprising either, though, because Bryce has been trying to figure her out since the last book, and she only scratched the surface. So much for being BFFs, am I right? I'm not gonna lie, I'm pretty irritated with this dead lady. I get Danika's need to protect her best friend, but to keep this many secrets from her, it's like she didn't trust Bryce at all. If it's somehow revealed that Danika has been alive all along, somehow, I would be surprised, but not that surprised. Although, that scene at the end of HOEAB feels pretty definitive. No one can be sure with Sarah, though. If she wanted to she'd figure something out. January 2024: Second re-read made me enjoy this a lot more than the first time. I still have beef with the rep and the annoying mer-fuckboi, but overall, it made a lot more sense to me this second time. February 2022: This book turned me into a clown 🤡 Spoilers ahead. . . . . . . . . . . BRYCE & HUNT “Our love is stronger than time, greater than any distance. Our love spans across stars and worlds. I will find you again. I promise.” Let me start by saying that I love them so much, they’ve become my whole personality. Bryce reminded me a little of Aelin with her scheming and secret plans. Luckily, it wasn’t as exaggerated as with Aelin, and it worked a lot better than in TOG. Her sense of humon was fantastic, I laughed so many times with her come backs. I loved how she called Hypaxia instead of Hunt because she needed some girl talk, she’s still one of the best characters Maas has written in that regard. Her female friendships are incredible. The conflict with Juniper, and that last phone call… god, my chest hurts just remembering. And once Juniper finds out what happened to her… can you imagine the angst? I can’t wait for CC3. Hunt Athalar is the best love interest Maas has ever written. There, I said what I said. I loved him even more in this book. He was simping for Bryce in a way that just got to me. I love my big, himbo men to simp for their women. And Hunt knew how to worship our Queen Bryce. His backstory with Shahar felt sketchy, tho. It’s said in this book that he told her he loved her, but she never said it back. And in the first book, he explains how Shahar basically found him when he was in a fragile state after losing his mother, and she pretty much brainwashed him into the cause, to the point that he blindly followed her to their doom. It feels like she used him and manipulated him into believing what they had was special to make him do what she wanted. Bryce was the first person who really saw Hunt and fought for him and the way he marveled at this was so precious. I just feel very protective of Hunt. He presents this strong front, but inside he’s a marshmallow. I even liked his moments of mate-induced rage to protect Bryce. That shit was hot, I don’t even care. I’m here for it. Their smut was out of this world scorching hot. Hunt’s dirty talk was so filthy, it gave me tingles. But what a way to give a girl false expectations. Regular sex won't ever be enough after reading Bryce and Hunt having world-altering, tantric sex. I loved how they became a team but still struggled making decisions together, and how each kept their own agenda and motivations. It was really interesting to see them working through these conflicts and becoming closer because of it. I love that Maas is giving us an established couple this early in the books, it’s rare in romance and I know if someone can make this work, it’s this author. RUHN I’m completely infatuated with this man. It’s been a long time since I lusted this hard for a fictional character. Ruhn has me in such a strong chokehold, I’m willing to forget I'm a feminist for him. That's how bad I’ve got it. After my re-read of the first CC book, I realized Ruhn is most probably Maas’ least toxic male character ever. Think about it. He supports his sister, even if it means he’s losing power, titles or even his magic sword. He loves her above anything else. He’s there for her at all times. He’s also there for his friends. He wants to change archaic Fae traditions. He doesn’t say a single problematic thing about women. In fact, even when Ruhn has been a party boy who enjoys casual sex for a long time, he’s portrayed as always respectful and caring. And don’t get me started on his first chapter, where he’s enthusiastically going down on some random girl whose name he can’t even remember. But that doesn’t stop him from giving her the best orgasm of her life. ✨Ruhn thinking he’s the prince of nothing. ✨Ruhn getting sleeve tattoos to cover the scars left by the abuse he suffered as a kid from his father. ✨Ruhn saying it’s lady’s choice when it comes to sex. ✨Ruhn saying he loves his sister over anything else. ✨Just Ruhn. In conclusion your highness, Ruhn Danaan is a p*ssy eater, and he must be protected at all costs. RUHN & BRYCE “Ruhn looked at his sister and said softly, “You brought so much joy into my life, Bryce.” Their relationship was so beautiful in this book. I got emotional the first time Bryce gave him a hug and he was so surprised and happy. They have such a beautiful bond, and how they look out for each other was my everything. Outside the romances, this is my favorite relationship by far. When he said Bryce had brought so much joy into his life... I ugly cried, y'all. RUHN & “DAY” “You remind me that I’m alive,” she said, voice thick. “You remind me that goodness can exist in the world.” I had so much fun trying to figure out who Day was and Maas played me a fool several times. I was so sure she was Hypaxia at first. And I must admit I was disappointed. Then that scene with the “rough male” happened and I thought it was Celestina. And let me tell you, I didn’t see the chemistry there at all. But I was willing to give it a try because Night/Day were starting to become my fucking everything, alright? And then, the plot twist of the century hit me in the face so hard I needed half an hour to recover lol Their mind-sex scene was so good, I think I've re-read it 10 times already. But the best part was knowing Ruhn was gonna regret it once he knew who she was. I read the beautiful disaster that was their romance, dying for the moment he realized she was one of their enemies and how much that was going to hurt. And boy, did Maas deliver or what. Their last scenes together broke me, especially Lidia calling him through their mental link and he keeping her out... My chest was literally hurting as I read that. They are going to become my whole personality until we get CC3. BRYCE & DANIKA “Through love, all is possible. One last clue from Danika. To look where she’d stamped the phrase—right on this male.” Look, I’m conflicted. On one hand, I loved the plot twist of Danika keeping her mate a secret. But at the same time, Danika kept so many secrets from Bryce when she was alive, that you end up wondering if they were even friends. It just doesn’t make sense. Why didn’t she confide in Bryce? It seems like she didn’t trust her, like Danika thought Bryce was just this vapid, party girl who didn’t care about anything else. But then, why tattoo the Horn on her back? It just doesn’t make sense and it’s pissing me off. I loved their friendship in the first book, but I feel like it was ruined in this one. And I adored Danika but now I just don’t know what her deal is. It’s all very odd. THARION The audacity this man had was astonishing. If Tharion was a real man, he’d be a mansplainer who sits in the subway with his legs wide open and talks about “not all men.” Istg I wanted to kill him when he had the audacity to constantly whine in his POVs about his current situation. Poor guy had ended up forced into servitude to his queen after he fucked her daughter under false pretenses of love and a future together. Poor girl believed him and she thought they’d get married. And he spent 10 years engaged to her, playing along while he worked for her mother, doing whatever was necessary to survive. Only thinking of himself, without caring about the hurt he was causing his fiance. Sure, the River Queen is a sketchy bitch, but that doesn’t mean what he did was right. And the way he decided he was done in this book and how he broke the engagement was also so disrespectful and unnecessarily mean. He left her alone at that part to fuck a random girl. Wtf, Tharion? It didn't sit well with me either how he kept flirting with Bryce. I can understand some friendly banter, but he constantly crossed the line by talking about her underwear, her body or just asking for sexual favors as a joke. And then he even kissed her once "as a joke." And it's funny that some people are complaining about Hunt being an alphahole when he actually laughted at Tharion kissing Bryce. I was more jealous than Hunt, wtf? lol Then he realizes Cormac was on a suicide mission, and instead of helping him, he left when Cormac told him to, even though Tharion knew Cormac was going to die if he did. He ran away. The mothereffer. You know what, I hope the Vipe Queen makes him suffer. I’m sorry, I really can’t stand him. ITHAN Look, I wanted to love him. But for the most part, he just made me super uncomfortable with his silent pining for Bryce. Like, I don't care, Ithan. I love Bryce and Hunt. You can move the fuck on or you can fuck off, honestly. I just hated how he knew his brother Connor and Bryce had a thing, and Connor thought they were mates, and still he harbored feelings for her. I don’t know, I prefer Ruhn and his loyalty to his sister, over this slimy loser panting over his brother’s supposed mate. And the way he told Bryce about Connor believing they were mates after she and Hunt got together. Or how he tried to rile up Hunt about having to wait forever for Bryce to make a decision… Dude, just stop. Then he moved in with Ruhn, Flynn and Declan and things got better. Their friendship was cute and he started to have a real personality, which is always good. By the end of the book, I was liking him more but still, not my favorite by far. I’m hoping his plotline about the secret Fenrys heir makes me like him better. CORMAC What was the point of this character? lol At first I hated him. Then the plot twist was truly magnificent and I started loving him. He turned out to have better morals than most characters. His speeches about fighting for what’s right were incredible. His sad story with Sofie only made him more interesting. His last scene with Ruhn was so emotional... And then he went on a suicide mission. And no one gave a damn. I’m so mad 😅 CONCEPT OF MATES “His lightning flowed into her like a river, and he could have sworn he heard a beautiful sort of music between their souls.” First of all, I loved how Hunt and Bryce chose each other as mates, even before knowing if they were real mates. What Bryce told Hunt, about how if she had a mate, it was him, was so beautiful. Romance where they enthusiastically choose each other over everyone else is my jam. And it was so masterfully done in this book!! Anyway, I think it’s interesting how Maas expanded on the concept of Mates and how they work differently for each race or so they believe at least. In the end, mates seem to be half social construct and half magic. And that social construct is problematic af. Which reflects really nicely with our own social constructs when it comes to genre and love. So hey, I love this. CHOSEN FAMILY TROPE I’m a sucker for this trope, it’s on my top 3 favorite tropes ever. Almost all my favorite books portrait a chosen family. And Maas is really great at developing this trope. I’m just mad this book’s chosen family consisted on Bryce and other 8 dudes. One of them was her mate. Another was her BFF who had secretly had a crush on her for forever. Another was a dude who kept flirting with her, talking about her underwear and offering sexual favors. Another dude was her brother. Another dude was her first crush when she was a teen. Another was gay. And lastly, her fake-fiance and new character who ended up adding nothing to the plot, but okay. Are you seeing what I’m seeing? Maas surrounded Bryce in a garden of peens. Not only that, but several of these dudes openly lusted after her. Where are the female friends??? Remember she had two in the previous book? Anyone remembers Hypaxia? She didn’t even show up in the story until past the half mark. And sure, she tentatively joined the group, but it wasn’t the same as the others. Like, wtf is up with that? I’m not vibing with this shit, let me be real here. And sadly, I think it has something to do with my next point. LGBTI REPRESENTATION Oh my god. OH MY FUCKING GOD. I’m livid, y’all. I’m so angry and disappointed and frustrated and just—What the fuck, Maas??? Alright, let’s compare couples so it’s obvious where the problem is. There are 3 queer couples in this book. 1. Declan and his boyfriend Marc. They started dating in between CC1 and CC2 so we don’t get to see any of this. Marc is just there and Bryce explains briefly they’ve been dating for a month and that’s it. They don’t touch or have any type of intimate moment throughout the whole book. Not even once. There's nothing to indicate they're romantically involved. No chemistry or sexual tension between them. So what, are we expected to care about them??? Sarah J Maas surely didn’t. She didn’t even bother to throw us a bone to pick our interest. The worst part is that Marc shows up only when they need his legal advice, since he’s a lawyer. So it feels like the character was only created to help move forward the plot. He has no agency or really any type of personality, except for being there and saying a few lines related to laws. 2. Juniper and Fury. Their romance shows up a little bit more. The book starts with them happily living together. So there’s no tension or anything that could pick the reader’s interest there. Their romance is just done and over. At least they kiss once, I guess. They are barely in the story, even though they’re supposedly Bryce’s best friends. I’m just mad because the chosen family trope was so well done in this book but it was Bryce and 8 other dudes. All the female characters disappeared or barely showed up at all during the book. And sadly, Juniper and Fury suffered the consequences. So why should I care about them? If I never got to read how their romance happened and I don’t get to read about them now either. 3. Celestine and Hypaxia. Which was a really good plot twist, let me add. And at least they were caught having sex, even though no detail was giving except for a single boob being out in the open lol But sadly, that’s all we got. Apparently they love each other, and it’s sad because they can’t be together. And Celestine is willing to fuck up anyone for Hypaxia, but Hypaxia doesn’t know. So what will happen when she does? But is that enough for me to invest in their romance? Ehhh. Are you seeing a pattern here? Meanwhile, there are 4 straight couples: 1.Bryce and Hunt. They became mates and shared some truly beautiful scenes with epic love declarations and scorching hot smut. 2. Ruhn and 'Day'. Their romance is so well done, it overthroned anything and everything else in this book. Just check social media and how they’ve taken over. Everyone is obsessed, and rightly so because their story was really well done. 3. Ithan and the wolf mystic. So he finds this female alpha wolf who was sold as a mystic, and she turns out to be a lost Fenrys descendant. And he goes against everything to set her free. Their single scene together had more chemistry and added more mystery to the story than the 3 queer couples together. 4. Flynn and the dragon Ariande. They are surely going to serve us some epic enemies to lovers and honestly, I can’t fucking way. Her few scenes were enough to have me obsessed. Sarah J Maas is really good at writing romance, that’s the reason why we read her books. But she adds a few queer couples, and they develop off page and have only a few scenes together with zero chemistry in an 800 pages long book? It’s insulting. I’d rather she didn’t give in to the pressure to include representation in her stories if she’s going to do this. Why couldn’t Declan fall in love with one of the characters that we know and care about? There’s Ruhn, Flynn, Ithan, Tharion… They were all single, any of them could’ve been bisexual. But nope, they are all straight. And meanwhile Declan dates a random no one cares about. Why couldn’t we read about Fury and Jun joining their group? That way we could’ve read about their romance in detail. Hell, why couldn’t we get their POVs? You’re telling me I had to read Tharion whining nonstop and I couldn’t get Fury’s POV? How about Hypaxia’s POV? She didn’t mention her romance, only hinted at loving someone she shouldn’t. Why couldn’t we read her internal turmoil and longing for the woman she knows she can’t have? Meanwhile Maas gave us hints at Hypaxia and Tharion having a thing for each other in CC1 and even in this book, to then reveal she’s in love with a woman. Like, wtf? ENDING AND MULTIVERSE The way I sobbed for a solid ten minutes after reading the ending. I’m so friking excited about this crossover. I don’t even know which book I want to read first, CC3 or ACOTAR5. And I can’t stop wondering how the eff is Maas going to pull this off. You know the amount of characters, storylines, relationships, conflicts, mysteries… there are if you combine both series?? Okay so here are some theories and thoughts I have about future books: . . . . . . So does this mean Rhys is related to Ruhn? But not Bryce… So 1. Could Rhys’ last name be Danaan?? and 2. Could Ruhn’s mother be Rhys’ sister? Also, teleporting is basically winnowing. They both master shadows and mind communication. They share the same powers and look alike. So obviously, I’m not okay??????? Is the creature trapped under the lake in ACOTAR the 7th Asteri? Was Amren working with the Asteri and once they left the ACOTAR world, she was left behind, thus why she was held prisoner?? Are the Fae in the CC world the Dusk Court that disappeared from the ACOTAR world?? Apollion said Hunt was bred, does that mean he could be Illyrian? Was he bred in preparation for the Starlight being born again? Because his powers charged Bryce and they could share energy and level each other up. So it seems like it was done intentionally if he was bred, since the Asteri need Bryce to open up the portals to conquere other worlds. Could the Viper Queen be a Valg? And what she did to Tharion was a blood-oath. Like Maeve did with Rowan, Lorcan, Fenrys…? Was the metheore mentioned in CC2 mothereffing Aelin???? . . . . . . . If you got this far in my review, I’m so very sorry. lol

House of Sky and Breath is a masterful continuation of the Crescent City series, delivering a complex and gripping narrative that keeps you hooked from beginning to end. This book picks up a few months after the events of "House of Earth and Blood," with Bryce and Hunt laying low on orders from the Asteri Rigelus. Their romance is blossoming, and Bryce is coming to terms with her newfound status as a Starborn Fae Princess with the power of Starlight. The story takes an intriguing turn as Bryce is suddenly betrothed to the Avallar Fae Prince Cormac, a move driven by political motives and her fear of her tyrannical father, the Autumn King. Meanwhile, the mystery of the missing human siblings, Sofie and Emile, unfolds. These siblings may hold a powerful secret related to their ability to control electricity, making them essential in the ongoing human-led Ophion rebellion against the Asteri. The narrative introduces a host of new and fascinating characters, each with their own unique backstories and motivations. As you follow Bryce and Hunt's journey, you'll also become engrossed in the unfolding Ophion rebellion, the complexities of Fae politics, and the profound secrets hidden within the Asteri Archives. The revelations about the Asteri's true nature and their exploitation of worlds add depth to the story, challenging the characters' understanding of the world they inhabit. Throughout the book, the chemistry between Bryce and Hunt deepens, and they come to realize the significance of their bond as mates, a concept in Fae culture that goes beyond traditional marriage. Their relationship is both passionate and tender, making their characters all the more engaging. Sarah J. Maas weaves a rich and intricate tapestry of storytelling, blending romance, action, political intrigue, and revelations about the nature of their world. House of Sky and Breath also leaves readers with a tantalizing cliffhanger, leaving you eager for the next chapter in this spellbinding series. In conclusion, House of Sky and Breath is an enthralling continuation of the Crescent City series that will keep fans of fantasy and romance eagerly turning the pages. It's a must-read for those who appreciate complex world-building, well-developed characters, and a story that never loses its momentum.

Warning: spoilers for all SJM books. Also, I'm pretty pissed off about this, so be warned and don't @ me. Save your tears for the pillow. I have never DNF'd an SJM book before. Never. I didn't even DNF Tower of Dawn, and that book was so fucking boring. I say that as someone who will gladly sit and watch the full 8 Hour Birds Bonanza with my cat. I say that as someone who enjoyed and even reread parts of Public Law by Mark Elliot and Robert Thomas (4th edn., Oxford University Press 2020). I like to sit and watch the fire. I don't need explosions and car chases. I am not a high-key person by any stretch of the imagination. But this book was on another level. It was so fucking dry. I tolerated Tharion's POV the first time, became enraged by it the second, and by the time we arrived at his third POV chapter, I shut the book because I just could not take it any more. How the HELL am I supposed to care about this character. Tell me that. And it's not just him. Tharion is the worst offender, being completely and utterly irrelevant in every sense of the word, but I cannot believe - nay, cannot stomach the fact that a good 80% of this book is spent hanging out in Bryce's apartment. There are people in concentration camps (and SJM is very keen to remind us that the people in those camps are humans, and humans are stupid petty ugly bastards who deserve to be oppressed because they're so ugly and dumb and they should be on their knees thanking Bryce and her sexy oppressor friends for deigning to treat them with the bare minimum of compassion, and never mind that Hunt spent years torturing them and other marginalised people in order to save his own chiselled backside, and now he's sad and his sexy sadness means it's fine that he put his wellbeing above the wellbeing of thousands of other people and he doesn't have to lose a wink of sleep over the fact that he mutilated people for his own gain. That's okay. Don't worry about it. Nothing to see here) and a whole war is going on and there are angels and demons and other dimensions and a whole bustling city outside, and yet here we are, flattening our arses on Bryce's couch like it's April 2020. Are you taking the actual piss with this. I have no idea what happened here. I don't know how we went from Aelin standing by her principles and unashamedly condemning those who had power yet did nothing to intervene during a genocide... to this. Aelin was furious at the powerful people in Adarlan who allowed the slaughter of the Fae and the magic-wielding humans and she was firmly on the side of the oppressed. So how did we end up here, courting this toothless, frankly insulting argument of "well, all sides are equally bad". No, they aren't. No. Slaves who kill their masters are not murderers. Concentration camp inmates who fight back against those locking them away behind barbed wire fences are not the agitators. Polite resistance is useless in the face of violent oppression. Telling people who are being violently oppressed to be nicer to their oppressors is absolute filth and I won't stand for it. I'm so tired of this: we saw it in ACOTAR, when the formerly slaveowning Fae had the gall to look the humans in the eye and say "why are you oppressing us". They are not oppressing you, Rhysand. You simply no longer have the power to treat them like objects. You are no longer allowed to break into their homes and force them to humiliate themselves for your own amusement. For privileged people, having the playing field levelled often feels like oppression, but it isn't. It just means you no longer benefit from the subjugation of others. Now you've gotta actually make an effort to be seen as remarkable. Which Rhysand isn't. He's just an anti-choice dickhead who sucked the soul out of his wife. With that said, at least ACOTAR had a bit of sparkle. It wasn't dry as old bones. All I can say is that, despite her many flaws, at least Aelin never turned into a pick-me Karen like Bryce and Feyre. Rowan wasn't the most exciting love interest, but nor was he a controlling fuckhead. But the biggest problem, with the ACOTAR books from ACOWAR onwards (don't even get me started on ACOFAS, where Rhysand busted a nut when Feyre showed him an image of their baby boy; get that child away from him and lock him the hell up, already) and with CC, is that there is no editor. Not a single editor, or at least not one that was awake, glanced over these pages. I already went into the hot mess that was the mystery plot in CC1 in my review, but holy fuck this book is even worse. Just page after page of contentless irrelevant waffling that I couldn't give less of a damn about. Like I said: ACOTAR had some magic about it (noncery, nepotism, and anti-choice bullshit aside) and TOG had a fun, engaging, if sometimes melodramatic and slightly messy plot. Despite its flaws, I actually still love TOG. I also still love ACOTAR, even though it's technically awful. I would still, if a little less so lately, consider myself a fan of SJM's work, and god knows I've put the time in. I've been following this author for ten years. I know all the trivia. I know all the lore. Feel free to test me. I just can't help but feel that SJM is taking advantage of her own increasing popularity, in that she's getting lazier and lazier with these shite plots and boring villains and horrible, horrible characters. Every single person in CC is vile, and not in a fun "man, these people suck and it's so much fun to watch them cause havoc" way. They're horrible, but the book is completely oblivious to it. The book presents them as heroes who deserve to have the rest of the world bowing at their feet. But they don't, and it creates this sort of weird cognitive dissonance, where the characters are acting in ways that any normal person would despise them for, but everyone within the story is praising them. If Bryce acted the way she does in my community, around the people I know, she'd have her shite on the doorstep and told to fuck off. To boot, her boyfriend is like if a piece of plain white bread was a person. Just the most milquetoast fucker. I also love how Ruhn's "I'm the end of my bloodline" thing actually comes to nothing, and he's just like "I don't know why the Oracle said that..." when the obvious choice would have been to make him gay. Or even to just make his mate a cis man. Did that not occur to anyone? Especially for Ruhn, for whom it would create conflict with his traditional father? Like, what is going on, here? Hello?? Knock knock?? Is anyone awake in the editing room? Are you asleep at your computer, SJM? Why do you keep missing these character opportunities and instead choosing the most boring option possible? "Bryce and Hunt are mates" Why the fuck is Bryce's mate not Aidas? Why is Reid Redner, who was in the first fucking book, not the Thunderbird, or at least a POV character with a view into the humans' world, and why are we not watching his business collapse under pressure from the racist Asteri, and why is that not the driver for our main Vanir characters to question their views about humans? Can Bryce not reflect on the privilege she has, which allows her to mouth off in front of police officers, or even to DATE police officers? Why are we just defaulting to the path of least resistance, every single time? "Extremely powerful, hot, capable people struggle with their power and hotness" is such an asinine basis for a story. I don't care. I'm not going to pretend to care. And I hate that this is seriously making me question whether I should bother reading any of SJM's work in the future. What's the point? It's all just a rehash of the same old story with the same old characters reskinned, void of nuance. Across SJM's bibliography, there are some real gems: as mad as it sometimes makes me, because the characters act cuckoo-bananas, ACOMAF is still great; Heir of Fire, Queen of Shadows, and Kingdom of Ash are also an absolute serve. I even love the first ACOTAR book, especially since it's the only one that really holds onto its atmosphere of deep Celtic Fae trickery. There's also a weird amount of poop, blood, and vomit, which is kind of audacious for SJM if you're familiar with her tendency to doll her characters up like celebrity Sims in Del Sol Valley. What else is there? ACOWAR reads like it was edited by a chimpanzee of above-average intelligence, but there's some good in there. I always liked Bryaxis, and Ianthe getting smoked by the Weaver was pretty cool. ACOFAS is dogshit and so is ACOSF, and the first TOG book is a bit gaudy and silly, but it's still fun, and I liked Crown of Midnight too for its twisty nonsense. Empire of Storms is batshit, but I didn't hate it. With all this considered, it feels like a defeat to give up on this book. To step away from this author and admit that we're not vibing anymore. I used to look forward to SJM's new releases, picking apart interviews, chatting with other fans on the subreddits, making theories, and even placing preorders. But now everything's changed. I can't even finish this book. God. How depressing is that. FIN
