When you manage your expectations by being realistic and enjoy tf outta this masterpiece 😌🤭 SPOILER FREE REVIEW I honestly feel so emotional finishing this book, saying goodbye to Bryce and Hunt's story. I was thoroughly entertained, invested and satisfied with the way this book was written. I would say that when you go into this book, please keep in mind you're reading Bryce's story, simply put you are going in for Captain Marvel and not Avengers Endgame 🤷‍♀️ I also see people disappointed with the way Bryce was in this book. Even though she had few moments where I felt frustrated with her, I fully understood her. In a strange environment, she is not going to or supposed to act calm. She will be paranoid. Meeting new people whom SHE doesn't know and acting suspicious, trying to escape makes ABSOLUTE sense. Even in her irrational actions, there were rational intentions 👀 Coming back to the book which is divided into Part 1, Part 2 and Part 3 like any other Crescent City book. Part 1 explored more folklore, history, new places and people (for Bryce) and setting up a much more powerful world building. I found myself loving it, there were some big reveals and connections. I was also shocked to see one of the creatures back in the world and it brought intense memories. It also ends on a brutal note. Iykyk. Part 2 was more hands on action, it built on to the reveals made in part 1 brilliantly. I see MANY people saying that this part bored them and dragged on. On the contrary, I found it to be much more intense and mind blowing. Lidia and Ruhn carried it beautifully. Part 2 ends on a very nerve wrecking note, and you'll immediately want to binge the rest of the book. Part 3 was simply put- Binge worthy. Big reveals happen here, characters in this world get what they deserve and I ate it up. Ithan and Bryce were my favorite here, and surprisingly Jesiba too. It ends on a satisfying note and I just can't wait to see how it's going to add up to the future books. Onto the characters- ❤️‍🔥Bryce- Although a bit erratic her actions are completely justified imo. She is the same Bryce we have grown to love- smartass, funny, badass, always standing up for the right and calculating. The sacrifices she's willing to make was emotional to see. But like any other, she does have flaws and is imperfect. ⚡Hunt- My man. The way he cared for Bryce was everything. Even while getting tortured to the point where he is close to death, all he cared about was Bryce and his friends. He would do anything to protect them, even if it means he's gonna end up hurt. His big reveal was one that I was never expecting and I was shook. I loved seeing him unleash and put Celestina in her place. 🔥Lidia- I LOVE her. She did so much for literally everyone good in this book, such huge sacrifices. She did not put herself first once and I loved her. I swear I just want to give her the biggest hug. 🖤Ruhn- Loved seeing the way he felt for Lidia. Man's had me gasping, crying, emotional for more. His bond with Hunt and Baxian was intense and so loyal. The way he was protecting Bryce was everything. Tho that one scene made me dizzy (you know which one). 🐺Ithan and 🧜‍♂️Tharion- Although different paths, I found them to be quite similar with the way they deal with their struggles. Before anyone gets frustrated with these two- Have you ever made a mistake and in order to correct it desperately, you make more bad decisions and more mistakes?? That sounds pretty relatable to me. Not all of us are perfect. Living in self loathing, guilt, and anxiety isn't easy. Tharion and Ithan thinking that they don't deserve anything good happening to them after making so many mistakes is real and it's a mental health representation at its best. So many people acting like Tharion and Ithan were annoying breaks my heart cause I found them to be so endearing and loving, so loyal, so worthy despite what the two thought. I just wish to hold them and talk to them about it all. Baxian- All I'll say is he has strong teeth 😭 Jesiba and Hypaxia- I appreciated so much what these two did, especially Jesiba. Without giving too much away, am sure you'll like them more. The romances- Bryce and Hunt- Honestly, after Feyre and Rhys these two are my favorite SJM couple and they are immensely underrated. Even in their arguments, they know when to support each other. They're the couple who will support each other in public even if they are wrong and correct the other in private. Ruhn and Lidia- So angsty. It's like they broke my heart multiple times and mended it to complete perfection. Literally everything about them is PERFECT. I loved how they communicated and bared themselves to each other. Also, did SJM throw in the marriage of convenience trope? 👀 Y'all gotta find out for which couple, no spoilers here. 🤭🤭 I believe people have forgotten that this is Bryce's story. In order to enjoy this book, you gotta keep that in mind. I can already see that SJM has foreshadowed a lot of multiversal possible scenarios. Hopefully she'll explore them on an Endgame level someday. But for now, am excited to see where the Crescent City series will go from here 😉 I highly recommend reading this series after ToG and ESPECIALLY ACOTAR. I did not want this to end, I could still read another 500 pages of this beautiful book and world. Already can't wait to reread 😭❤ •~•~ IT'S FINALLY HERE 😍😍 In all it's glory 🥹🥹 ~•~•~ Am so ready for Jan 2024

The weakest conclusion to an SJM series by far. This book was one big deus ex machina clusterfuck. But I think most fans will overlook the huge issues in this book because we get to see some old favourite characters. Let's start off with the good parts: - Lidia Cervos 🧎🏻‍♀️🧎🏻‍♀️🧎🏻‍♀️Few characters had any agency in this book. Lidia was one of the few people who actually made a difference in this book. She really stole the show from Bryce and Hunt. - In the same vein as Lidia, Nesta lit up every scene she was in. Every scene she was in, I only noticed her. She really carried every part of the story she touched and she is so fun. - And obviously the entire Prythian part because those characters are elite. Loved the lore drop we got. - There was a particular scene with a few characters waving at each other that broke my heart. Now on to the bad: - Welcome to the Bryce Quinlan Show, where I spent 50% of the book asking myself "Why are Tharion/Flynn/Declan/Sathia/Hunt/Ruhn even in this scene??". So much of this book involved Bryce and Co. going somewhere to do something. But they all could have been Bryce's solo missions because it literally would not have made a difference if her companions weren't there. I think this was made particularly evident because there were 3 or 4 times where Bryce had to relay stuff she had done in the previous chapters to her group of friends. Because her friends weren't doing anything. The side characters felt soooo unnecessary in so many points in this book. - Another note on Bryce, she has some smart moments in the book but so much of her dominance is because she is The Chosen One. Everything she gains is because she is related to XYZ and has ABC in her blood. It makes it really hard to root for her because she didn't have to earn anything. - As I already mentioned in HOSAB, Bryce is only interesting in the context of Danika. By herself, she isn't that particularly interesting or someone I would root for. I think the strongest part about her was her friendship to Danika. This is particularly evident when anything happens between Hunt and Bryce. They just don't have that much chemistry tbh. I really wish this series had been about Bryce and Danika. Hunt really felt like a side piece. I really dgaf about this man. - I can't believe I had to read about Hunt going commando because his d**k is too big to fit into his underwear. I actually wanted to gouge my eyes out. 🤢😵‍💫😵 Also Hunt and Bryce getting handsy while their friends were fighting for their lives? Why were Ruhn and Lidia trying to get it on while their friends were literally right beside them in the cave? The most unnecessary scenes that were added just so this book can be spicy. - Ithan LOLOLOL. If you look up "filler character" he would be the #1 offender. He actually didn't do anything in this book for the first 70% and then he suddenly just have everything happen to him. His rise in power was the most eye-rolling experience because he doesn't deserve any of this. - Tharion sorry babes I wish I had skipped every scene you were in. I actually do not give a fck about this man. Suddenly Sathia appears. What did she even add to the story? Tharion and Ithan were the two most ridiculous characters in this book. I'm actually so mad both of them got so much "screen time". But Tharion might get the "Nesta" treatment because it is clear his story isn't over. - In true SJM fashion, we get the "We could have told you all of this in Book 1 but you weren't ready so we are just going to explain everything now". I'm so sick and tired of important information being gatekept for the sake of having a plot. - I want SO MUCH MORE grovelling between Ruhn and Lidia. I wanted the angst and yearning and the hurt x comfort. They are by far the best couple in this series. - LOOOL COOPER. Why did we focus so much on Sophie and Emilie in book 2 for them to basically not matter at all. - Sigrid and Ariadne felt like loose ends. Perhaps they will be important in future books but they took up too much time in this book for them to not matter much at the end. - OK, so book 1 had that big dramatic massacre, which really got my hopes up that SJM would actually commit to some gruesome ends for some of her main characters. SYKE! I'm so tired of none of the characters actually being in danger. - Hypaxia exists to be a deus ex machina. Her and Jesiba's sole purpose in the series is to get people out of a pickle. They literally didn't serve any other purpose. - Also where were Juniper and Fury? They were completely neglected except for one scene. - While writing this, I just remembered I haven't even mentioned Baxian. That just shows how insignificant he was in every scene he was in. He just gets lumped in with Hunt and Co. - The Harpy comes back for her to get KO'd in 0.2 seconds? - Hypaxia defeats a certain character very quickly. It felt so out of left field and rushed. Overall, this book felt sloppy.

The harder you rise, the harder you fall. Sarah J Maas wrote her own kill switch to the “Maasverse” and activated it when this was published. Disappointed does not even sum up the entirety of how I’m feeling. For those people who are really enjoying and loving this, I am so happy for you, and I wish that was the case for me. But I am just glad to have finished it so I never have to think about it again. Long live the Crescent City duology. I am envious of the characters who got to die in HOSAB/HOEAB so they didn’t have to experience HOFAS and the defamation of character that touched every single character I had previously cared about and rendered them boring, two dimensional and soulless. For a book “millions of fans” have been waiting for for two years, Sarah did not deliver. She did not even purchase a postage label. The epic conclusion to the crescent city trilogy, which had so much potential, was reduced into a messy concubine of soap opera, unwanted comedy and minimal stakes. There was so much potential. So much potential and this is what we got. I am so angry. The writing in this book leads me to believe Sarah no longer cares about Lunathion, or her characters. This book is a testament to laziness, loss of passion and the arrogance of knowing no matter what she wrote, she would be making money. Through love all is possible… yet there was no love in this book. It was rendered impossibly cold and distant from anything else she could have possibly written. Through “convenient coincidences”, all is possible, should be her new slogan. I don’t even understand how in any stage of production, anyone at bloomsbury could confidently look at this and not question the drastic changes to characters, such as Bryce’s complete tyrannical selfishness, and Hunt’s stripped down personality and so on and so on. HOFAS was a failure and nothing more. Due to my disappointment at the entire picture, I could not even bring myself to be excited when certain plot points; which I would have screamed at, were unravelled, they felt anticlimactic and convenient at best. The the potential Sarah carefully constructed in not only the last two books, but the small sprinkles of lore throughout all her books, remains completely untapped and unused. Fans and theorists could have patched together a better ending to this series and (as someone who grew distasteful of theorists and did not look forward to a crossover) I’ve seen theorists who care more and know more and understand more of Sarah’s precious worlds than she seemingly did in this book. I am so so so angry. Sarah chose convenience, palatable and cheap shock factor over writing something meaningful. I can only guess this comes from the fact that “fame” has gotten to her head. Sarah has done a disservice to long standing fans in an attempt to suck in and appeal to celebrities and influencers, blending epic backstories and well planned out history into grey palatable mush that can be consumed by the masses, instead of the quality book it could have been to be consumed by the people that make this all possible for her. Even her regular fashion of fast paced, “epic” final 100 pages could not overcome first 700 pages of convenience, low stakes nonsense. There was no slice of life, no character development, just a long endless cave of info dumping and convenience. Sarah’s best writing is a footnote in the past. Bloomsbury I am so so disappointed in you for allowing this, marketing this, profiting off this. House of Flame and Shadow is a mockery of everything good in fantasy and did not deserve our excitement, our hope, or our joy. I normally restrain myself from negative reviews, because I do believe all art is subjective and everyone has a right to enjoy art as it comes. But this was objectively bad and there are no excuses. There is no explanation. Someone as revered as Sarah J Maas should be doing better as she rises, not worse. I hope HOFAS/Sarah and the rightful people at bloomsbury receive the criticism this book deserves so that they can ensure future books do not suffer the same fate.

I'd like to formally request that Bryce make her grand re-entry to Midgard riding Helion's pegasus. . . Ok well that ⌃⌃ didn’t happen, but it doesn’t matter because this book absolutely slapped. Honestly, it’s so hard to compare SJM books with others out there, because her writing is in a unique lane of its own. I applaud her (yet again) for her ability to weave so many threads, characters and mythology into one insanely action packed tale. SPOILERS BELOW . . . I'm going to start with Bryce. I adore her. I feel like the theme of this book was ‘Level Up’, and she did this and then some. After all of the shit she went through in the previous books I loved see her step fully into her own. I’ve seen a few reviews criticising her character as being ‘insufferable’, which I find kind of interesting … mostly for the fact that when we judge something, it’s most often the thing that we don’t give ourselves permission to be or feel, or are judging within ourselves. As a collective, women have been taught to fear our own power, and here we’re presented with a fully fleshed, whole person that doesn’t feel the need to humble herself or shrink to make herself more relatable to others. Given the above, I get this can be polarising for some people who identify as female… but for me? I freaking LOVED this. The scene in particular between her and the two fae kings was so cathartic. SJM was really channelling some feminine rage and putting a metaphoric foot down against the patriarchy. Honestly, the amount of times I wish I’d been in a position to fight back like this… it was so wonderful to read. Bryce’s character arc across all three books felt right to me. The bit of tension between her and Hunt also felt valid - I could see things from both their sides and it felt true to their characters. Ultimately, Bryce was carrying the sole weight of being the key to destroying the Asteri, and her mental fortitude (while maybe it came across as being too headstrong at times) was needed in order for her to carry this out. Sorry not sorry. Onto Hunt - bless him, he really went through it in this book. I also thoroughly enjoyed his ‘Level Up’ towards the end. The romantic tension between he and Bryce was definitely higher in books 1 & 2 - here they were more in the ‘marriage phase’ of being a couple, which I guess is fine… although I wish we’d had a little bit more of a dramatic reunion / spice. Overall Hunt has always been a solid character in my mind. Lidia & Ruhn… I LOVE. They carried the romance in this book. Lidia was an incredible personality to work into the mix - she kind of reminds me a bit of Manon in that she’s not the FMC, but easily could be. Ithan - his scene with Connor had me sobbing. I had secretly hoped he’d end up as the Prime! Nesta - I’ve never been a massive fan of hers, but I was surprised by how much I enjoyed her in this book!. All of the snark and banter between her and Bryce was fantastic. Azriel - honestly, I’ve never gotten much from Az, and this book was no different. I think people project onto his personality (which is very quiet) and build stories about him in their own minds, because in reality we know very little about him, and he doesn't really speak that often. That being said, I loved the sweet moment between him and Nesta when he convinced her to take off the mask - it did mushy things to my heart. THE ENDING I have no words except… what in the holy Interstellar!!? SJM can sure write a mind blowing action scene. So. Freaking. Amazing. THE ACOTAR CROSSOVER For the most part, I was OK with how this panned out. There was always going to be a fine line between this remaining a Crescent City book vs turning into an ACOTAR take over. I think I would have liked just a **smidge** more from the interactions between Bryce and the gang - particularly with Rhys, Cassian and Feyre (who did not make an appearance at all.) It honestly felt like a Nesta x Crescent City crossover in the end, but I’m not mad about it. I am glad SJM stuck with the Crescent City POVs and that it stayed firmly a CC book. Furthermore, now that she has opened the connection between the two worlds, it leaves room for CC characters to cameo in future ACOTAR books which I wouldn’t object to in the slightest. And with the Starsword now back in Velaris… I’m sure it will come into play in future books. Side note: Randall & Ember’s bonus chapter - IDK why, but she continues to portray Rhys as an overbearing asshole? I just want the Rhys we know and love back. THE NEXT CRESCENT CITY BOOK I’d guess it will be a continuation of Tharion’s story. His journey in this book, was, essentially a retelling of The Little Mermaid - it would make sense for the next book given House of Many Waters is the remaining title. I think SJM put Tharion through the ringer in this book to lay the groundwork for a lot of character growth and redemption should his story continue. Maybe he and Ariadne are going to wind up together?? Ithan's romance was also hinted at with Perry, but again there's a wide open space there so that's also another possibility. TO SUM UP I'm really sad this series is over, I've loved every second of it. <3

SJM has somehow managed to completely capture my heart and blow my mind once again! I want to start by saying that SJM never fails to completely capture my heart. Some books I may love just a tiny bit more but there is no doubt that I have loved everything she has written. With House of Flame and Shadow I was pulled in immediately and in a complete choke hold. I did not want to move! Not to eat, work, or even talk to anyone. Like, hello. Leave me alone, I'm in Midgard right now. Often I find that there's a slow build with SJM books. Nah lol. Not with this one. From page one it is off to the races I had to actually steal moments to catch my breath, stare at the ceiling for a little bit. Do my best to collect myself and then just jump right back in. It is so addictive and fast paced! It was consuming, exciting, riveting, an edge of your seat, nail biting thrill ride!! In the first two books there were times I would get a little lost with the plot because, let's be honest- there's A LOT going on but with HOFAS I felt that the story was very clear and concise. its been several years since i fully immersed myself in all of SJMs books, so my rose-colored glasses have started to fade a bit since then. before, i would have given this 5 stars, no questions asked. but now, im a bit harder to please. but there was a lot about this that did please me! at the end of the last book, my main concern was how the crossover was going to work, and this exceeded my expectations. i thought it was handled very well and felt as natural/seamless as it could. i enjoyed how it further built the crescent city world, but also supported the world building in ACOTAR. i also really liked how everything is concluded (im assuming this is the final book?). everything is wrapped up perfectly, all the character arcs are fulfilled nicely, and all the pieces of the story fall right into place. that being said, this could have used some tighter editing. there was a lot of repetition and unnecessary filler scenes, which made several sections of the story drag. the constant narrative/POV shifts within a chapter often felt jarring and, at times, pointless. so there were quite a few moments when i felt myself being taken out of the story because of these things. i do think, from a concept standpoint, this book is pretty exceptional and high in entertainment value. but, from a writing perspective, i didnt quite feel like this is SJMs best finished product. but that wont stop me from still reading whatever she writes. lol. ↠ 4.5 stars

I have a love hate relationship with this book. There were so many things I liked about it, yet a lot of stuff bothered me too that left me feeling perplexed. Despite my mixed feelings, I was completely engrossed the whole time and enjoyed it. It genuinely makes it hard to rate the book 🫠 I’m leaning towards 3.5 stars. It's not to say it was a bad book; it’s just not what I thought it’d be, and it gave a completely different vibe to CC1&2. Spoilers ahead!! - - - - - The book is extremely plot driven, and I loved learning about the universe’s lore! I don’t think I’ll ever wrap my head around everything revealed. How Sarah can think up these ideas and craft such intricate worlds, I have no idea!🤯 Part 1 was intense! The crossover was amazing. I appreciated how the book remained a Crescent City book and wasn’t wholly overpowered by the crossover. However, I didn’t like that too much was revealed all at once, too quickly, and mainly through direct dialogue. It would have been better if Bryce had discovered things on her own instead of being told straight up. It was almost a little too convenient. It set the tone for the rest of the discoveries as well. Nothing was played out entirely to its full potential. The lore was amazing, there’s no denying that, but the execution of it could have been better. It felt flat and almost like a tick box exercise, unlike Sarah’s usual style. With the number of things that were revealed, it might have been better to split this into two books as it sometimes felt rushed. I can’t get over the fact that this entire book's timeline was ONE WEEK! If it could have been spread further, it would have worked so much better, and that way, it would have addressed the lack of depth. My main dislike of the book was the complete lack of emotional connection. All the characters lost the usual flair they had in CC1&2. It was as if they all lost their personalities. And maybe that’s with it being plot driven, but something just felt off with them all, and there was a sort of emptiness to them. It’s the complete opposite of CC1&2. Those books had me sobbing, but with this one, I didn’t find it anywhere near as emotional as I thought it would be or what it attempted to be. My issues with this started to present during part 2, with the reunion of all the characters. It was so underwhelming. We know Sarah likes her POV switch ups, and I usually don’t mind it in any of her books, but something was off here. The switches were abrupt and often within the same chapter, so any emotional development happening instantly fell short, and I struggled to immerse myself. Not to be picky, but there were many grammatical errors, too. I found many missing quotation marks, which just ended up disrupting the flow even further, as I was like 'wait, when did the dialogue start?' On the other hand, I didn’t find myself getting bored in anyone’s storyline since it was extremely fast paced. It was hard to find a good point to put it down as the plot and the story just never stopped! Bryce frustrated me so much! She almost felt like a completely different character, and her character arc was extremely messy and frankly made no sense. She was acting as if she knew everything and was so unserious. Thankfully, part 3 is where she starts to return to her usual self, and by the end of the book, I was thinking 'there’s the Bryce I know and love'. But the arc she went on to get to that point was bizarre. Bryce and Hunt’s relationship is part of what made me love CC so much, but their relationship in this book was flat. It lacked the chemistry, banter, and warmth they usually had. Sarah, why on earth did you have them arguing after their reunion!?!?!? Why were they constantly at odds with each other? I thought they had resolved their trust issues in CC2, so I did not like the angst between them at all. I get that they’re portrayed as a real couple, but I’m sad at how it played out 😭 They just needed to talk to each other and explain their feelings, but it was instantly shut down whenever they tried. That was primarily due to Bryce - I don’t understand why she acted as she did towards Hunt; she constantly dismissed his feelings. And again, the abrupt POV changes did not help. I’m glad they returned to normal in part 3, and I’m happy I got the bonus chapters between them to end it on a good note. Ruhn and Lidia were certainly a highlight!! There were loads of reveals about Lidia, which were completely unexpected. It made me love her even more. I must admit their relationship development felt awkwardly paced to me, though, which is such a shame because their romance journey could have been so much more beautiful 😭 Surprisingly, I enjoyed Tharion’s and Ithan’s chapters. They added a nice reprieve from the intensity and added some value to the journey towards the end. Part 3 saved the book for me and was the only part where I felt somewhat emotional, even though the ending was pretty convenient. At no point did I even fear for any character, as it just didn’t feel high stakes enough. Shahar’s appearance was such a lovely surprise. I loved the reveal of Brann’s name. I didn’t connect the dots with that one, so I jumped out of my skin at that!! The sprites were some of my favourite side characters, and the mentions of Lele were a nice touch too 🥺 The Hel plot was handled well, and the reveal of Hunt’s father was a great twist. Overall, I’m feeling pretty bittersweet about it. Part 1 was good, I didn’t entirely like part 2, and part 3 saved it. It set up the next ACOTAR book well, and I can see how the next CC book will play out too. ——————————————— HAPPY HOFAS RELEASE DAY 🥳 ——————————————— apparently the book has been leaked and people are posting spoilers of the ending on twitter/tiktok etc😭 thankfully I haven’t seen anything but just had to give you guys a warning to be careful!!! ——————————————— OMG we have a cover!!! EDIT: FULL REVIEW, CONTAINS SPOILERS AND LOTS OF THEM I am so unbelievably disappointed with crescent city 3 and I have a lot of thoughts I’m about to unpack, if you haven’t finished it yet do not scroll on - if you have finished it and too feel let down, scroll on and enjoy my rant. Obviously the cliffhanger from cc2 was huge and sure I was curious to see how it unfurled (and it did so in an incredibly predictable way), but my main priority?? Seeing Bryce and Hunt reunite. That is ALL I cared about. The PAIN those two went through at the end of cc2 - I needed a proper reunion. And what did we get?? We got a 2 page reunion where Bryce enters a room where everyone is else is not just Hunt, doesn’t even speak to hunt, they barely speak, SJM GAVE US NOTHING. NOTHING. THEY SAID A FEW WORds that was supposed to convey all they felt at being reunited and that’s it? I EXPECTED HUGE DECLARATIONS OF RELIEF AND LOVE AND SEX AND HAPPINESS AND I GOT 2 PAGES OF BASICALLY FUCK ALL. that was my first act gun for this book and really sets the tone for what’s to come. BRYCE WAS SO ARROGANT TO WHAT HUNT HAD BEEN THROUGH. OFC HE MIGHT HAVE SOME RESERVATIONS ABOUT YOU GOING OFF TO DIE WHEN HE CANT HELP??? DO YOU REMEMBER HIS PAST???? WHAT HE JUST WENT THROUGH SEEING YOU VANISH AND HIM UNABLE TO SAVE HER????? but Bryce threw a fit everytime he showed reluctance to go through with a not well thought out plan???? Sjm clearly didn’t know what to do with them to move their relationship forward, and for that I will always be disappointed. Any issues they had were resolved in stupid unmeaningful ways and I hate it because not enough time was given to them. I’m just feeling quite sad about it because I loved them the most out of all SJM lovers and I felt she had decided to move on from them like 100 pages in and idk the small bits we got were just not satisfying. Her teleporting to him bcos he’s her home? Love. Them not talking about anything because they have no page time? Fucking disappointing. There was time to take a beat and flesh out their reunion!!! there was no need to race to the next thing!!!! NOTHING is unpacked. EVERYTHING introduced is wrapped up by the next chapter. There is NO suspense. No drama. No stakes. I’m supposed to believe the Asteri are so so evil and unbeatable? How. When ofc Bryce had the solutions basically from chapter 2. Ofc she found a video from her ancestor explaining exactly what to do. There was no moral debate, no inner turmoil to be resolved - the stuff that was there was resolved too quickly for me to believe it. Bryce hates the Fae and doesn’t want to save anyone? Oop she changdd her mind bcos ofc she’s a kind person at heart. Fucking cop out. Because everything is neatly resolved quickly, this book becomes BORING. SJM has a very addictive quality to her writing, that hasn’t changed. But if you’re going to give me a million POV’s that switch MID CHAPTER, you need to give me a reason to care. Tharion is a whiny prat who is somehow so forgettable despite having so much on page time. His plotline is BORING. Actually all their plotlines are boring because there’s no suspense. For example, Ithan kills the stupid Fendyr heir (why even introduce that character she had zero purpose genuinely none ithan’s arc still would’ve flowed the exact same without her like he could’ve gone and killed Sabine once he had to antidote to unlock his powers) and she’s bought back to life basically immediately?? Like what the fuck?? If you need something to test a characters morality and growth, WHY UN-DO IT IMMEDIATELY. WHY GIVE US AS THE AUDIENCE MEANS TO DOUBT ITS SIGNIFICANCE. It would have been better to have more focused chapters that allowed for suspense - more time with each character so we’re left more in the unknown for the others. And I’m biased but GIVE ME MORE BRYCE AND HUNT. GIVE ME MORE RUHN AND LIDIA. Everyone else was boring and could’ve had their POV’s significantly cut. Also I’m sorry but Bryce not sharing her plan and everyone being like oh that’s fine she has a plan got tiring really quickly bcos part of Bryce’s charm was the fact she’s intelligent and a fast thinker on the spot, not really a planner idk. Felt a bit off. And her not sharing everything with Hunt? Broke me a bit. Over to the crossover - Nesta was a great choice for it. I never wanted a full crossover with the inner circle - crescent city 3 is SO DIFFERENT in tone and themes and just general vibes that too much time with the inner circle would’ve taken from that plot. to have only a couple characters as the focus was a smart move. I love my girl Nesta and she was excellent - it was a delight to see the powerful fae she is. I’ve always been meh over azriel so idc that much about his presence. I just don’t find him that entertaining idk. I think it was fun that Bryce needed something from their world for her fight, and I’m fucking so relived there was no Aelin crossover. To all those suggesting that, are you ok??? That would’ve made this book way too messy. I enjoyed the references to her world and was happy to leave it at that. Anything throne of glass related would need a whole new book, not a cameo!! And omg the little glimpse into cassian and nesta’s life filled me with joy. so I actually think the crossover was a huge pro to this book. The actual info from the crossover was a bit force feeding us information but whatever. A history lesson was kind of a boring way to do it. I’m not stupid so deliver information to me in a way that makes me curious and think and consider. I enjoyed the showdown between Bryce and Nesta and Azriel. But I think overall could’ve been done more interestingly. ESPECIALLY when Bryce takes that info back to the others. It was like ‘Bryce recounts what happened to these people’ ‘Bryce recounts what happened to another lot of people’ ‘Bryce decides to do this without thinking or speaking or actively engaging with anyone’. And she didn’t care enough about being reunited with Hunt idc what you all say SJM decided to lessen that trait of hers when Bryce in CC2 would NEVER. Lidia CARRIED this book but even then there was just not enough. This book suffers from too many POV’s moving too rapidly for me to feel any sort of satisfaction from them. I wish every plotline and character arc was more unpacked, and this was longer as a result and split into two books. Basically everyone’s fan theories were right, and it feels SJM gave up trying to shock or intrigue us - which I find lazy and just downright sad because I loved what crescent city set up. Along the way, everything in that got lost. Only redeemable thing was the ending - SJM writes a great battle scene. Finally some stakes where Hunt has to do something, Bryce and Hunt actually work together, and some redemption for Hunt. The overall plot is fine but delivered in such a boring, uninteresting way that I feel disappointed. Give me a longer book with more intrigue and interaction and maybe I’d be feeling different. This book was ultimately quite boring, which considering what needed to be done, was a surprise and a let down. Any info we needed was given to us immediately, any issue resolved quickly, any questions of power settled. And as a quinlar girlie, I just didn’t have enough of them - SJM clearly has her favourites and gave more attention to those. I have such mixed feelings about this book. There are things that I liked and things that I really didn't. I definitely liked it better than CC2, but the series has just never gotten close to touching how much I loved CC1. Throwing 3.5 stars on this for now I think. Some vague, non-spoiler thoughts: - Bryce and Hunt continue to be the saving grace of this series, I genuinely think they're pretty good characters to carry the main plot. - The crossover - the thing I was most worried about in this book - panned out pretty well I think. I appreciate the balance here and don't think it overshadowed that this is ultimately a CC book, not an ACOTAR book. - Approaching this as a multi-POV book, I'd say I enjoyed 3 of the 5 plotlines in this and hated 2. - The first book was really well carried by its side characters and then in books 2 and now 3 the side characters actively drag down the narrative and feel like they're only there to pad pages and make these books 800 pages for no reason. Someone explain to me why Tharion and Ithan, two huge idiots who add nothing to the narrative, are worth a POV and not someone like Fury, an interesting character we've veiled in mystery who could be actually useful and yet have severely under-utilized since the first book. - Info dumps. Pages upon pages upon pages of infodumps. Entire chapters of "sit down and take notes while I verbally explain all of this to you and also try to justify why I didn't explain any of this to you two books ago even though I absolutely could have." - Still vacillating on how I feel about Lidia's storyline. - A number of side plots that were either dropped entirely or tied up far too quickly, to the point that it feels like the side plot should have just been edited out. - The culmination of at least one large overarching plotline we've had going since book one played out very well. - But ultimately the ending is SILLY (truly there is no other word for it) and of course incredibly predictable in classic SJM fashion. I don't know why I ever expect anything different from her, she does the same thing in the same order every single time. I devoured this book in two days - largely to avoid spoilers - and while it kept me mostly pretty engaged for all of that because I was invested in where things were going, there were definitely severe lulls and entire POV characters that I dreaded seeing on page (Ithan and Tharion). As I said above, mixed feelings.

Alright. Now that I’ve taken an hour to stare at my ceiling and be depressed (that the book is over, that it was so terrible) I’m finally ready to write a review. I’ll demarcate the sections containing spoilers so if you haven’t read yet, you can skip those parts. Here goes. I am so sad to report this, but it feels like Maasverse is going the way of the MCU. Dragged down by its own lore, sagging under its own weight, CC3 was ultimately….. forgettable. All of the problems that I had with CC2 carried through into CC3. There were several plotlines that felt completely unnecessary to the overall arc of the story and only served to bloat the page count. Entire chapters were devoted to the sort of expository lore-building that I thought we were done with after CC1. Once I reached the halfway point of the book, I started skimming through chapters that felt irrelevant. For a book that promised to be so climactic and exciting, I should NOT have been able to do that without missing critical information, but every conversation and storyline began to blur together and feel exactly the same. I hate to say it, but too much of the time reading this, I was………… bored. The beating heart of CC1 was Bryce & Danika’s friendship. It formed an emotional throughline that made the ending, when Bryce made the Drop and Lehabah sacrificed herself, so impactful. That same emotional heft felt completely missing from CC3. I also thought it was missing from CC2, but there was such a dramatic payoff at the end of the book (“Hello, Bryce Quinlan. My name is Rhysand”) that I was willing to look past that. Now, after another book too heavy on lore and interweaving plotlines and too light on genuine character development outside of power level-ups, I feel my attachment to these characters fading, which is SUCH a disappointment. Finally, the third act of the book became so overwrought with RIDICULOUS plotholes and leaps of logic that it almost felt unreadable. There was no underpinning logic to keep the story rooted in a sense of reality, or a sense that there were rules at all. I feel like this is more a problem of editing than writing. It’s the editor’s job to question the logic of the world that the writer has created - to make sure the magic system and rules are airtight, so that it feels real. Based on the number of typos I caught while reading, I think this thing was barely edited at all. What a colossal disappointment. ******** SPOILERS BELOW************ Okay, if you’ve read the whole book then you’re probably thinking the same thing I am….. WHERE TF IS AELIN?! HOW COME WE ONLY GOT TWO SECONDS IN PRYTHIAN??? Maybe it’s on all of us for thinking this was going to be a full-blooded crossover, but I am SO disappointed by how little time we got with the ACOTAR characters!!! And the majority of that time, with Nesta and Bryce in the tunnels, was repetitive to the point of being boring. After such a COLOSSAL cliffhanger at the end of CC2, I cannot believe this is all we got. Now we wait another 2-3 years for ACOTAR 6…… Sarah, if you’re reading this, please fire your editor. I cannot go through this disappointment again.

The friends they’d made were what mattered in the end. Not the enemies. Through love, all is possible. Spice: 🌶️🌶️ I knew this book was going to alter my brain chemistry. It is so incredibly well thought out and complex. I always complain that I have to wait two or more years for each of her books, but given how intricate they all are, I actually find it weird that Sarah J Maas doesn't need more time for them. What's more, without spoiling anything, my favorite part is obviously the connections the Maasverse worlds have with each other. We all know there's a connection, but the way it all comes together had me screaming into the void in delight. Also, even if I hadn't seen SJM's interview about writing more Crescent City books in the future, this book would've been enough to answer those questions for me. She makes abundantly clear that she intends to write more stories in this world and I couldn't be more excited. Although, she emphasized that we won't be getting them any time soon. She'll probably let us sizzle like she did with A Court of Silver Flames. Possibly even longer than that. At least we're getting Azriel's book soon(ish). Furthermore, if I didn't already love Bryce Adelaide Quinlan, and I most definitely do, this book alone would do it. She is not the first in the list of SJM's badass and cunning female protagonists and she's not going to be the last. However, out of all three books in the series, this is the most delightfully clever she has ever been. She took on all those oppressors and sexist fuckers like a goddamn pro. Also, she has the most amazing comebacks out of all the other SJM ladies. I honestly think she could beat Aelin in a verbal duel. She does make some choices that feel a little questionable and a little too risky, and some that may or may not be a little redundant. Other than that though, she blew my mind. Moreover, Hunt has to be the unluckiest boy in all of Midgard. The poor guy just can't escape unrelenting pain and suffering. He's been through so much shit already, it's hard to see him go through it all over again. Seeing a character that you love so much get a glimpse of true happiness only to have it ripped from his grasp is always such a punch in the gut. Me eating it all up like it doesn't eviscerate my very being every single time is completely unrelated. At least Hunt actually has allies now. He has people who care about him and want to help him. In spite of his suffering and all the trauma, he still supports Bryce and her quest to overthrow the government, even if it terrifies him. Besides, we finally learn the truth of his origins, which is every bit as fascinating as any other revelation in the book. In addition, I adored the dynamic between Hunt and Bryce in this book more so than the other two. It is so refreshing compared to what I usually read from SJM as well as other romance authors. SJM did not follow the standard 'character A dropping everything immediately to save character B no matter the consequences'. Instead, both Bryce and Hunt acknowledge that protecting innocents is more important than protecting each other, but they also have true faith in the other's ability to protect and keep themselves alive. They both choose the greater good over their mate on several occasions and only after securing that do they help one another. None of this diminishes their feelings or how strong their bond is. On the contrary, it shows a deep understanding between them. They respect and follow the other's wishes instead of being selfish. Likewise, I loved Ruhn and Lidia's storyline. They have their own character development throughout the book, especially Lidia whose character is completely different from what we have known for most of the series. She is more than just The Hind. Her backstory is slowly unraveled throughout the book, and while it is a sad one, it is also my favorite bit of exposition in the book. (I can't tell you. You have to read it!) Sadly she is not easily accepted by Ruhn specifically after the revelation of her true identity, something she is desperate to resolve. For his part, Ruhn doesn't have as much character development as Lidia but her revelation shocks him and leaves him feeling betrayed on top of being captured by sadists. He doesn't take the news so well, therefore, most of his journey is to accept Lidia's Daybright side as well as her Hind side. I loved their romance just as much as I did Bryce and Hunt's, maybe even more so. It is a relationship in progress and it has a lot of interesting ups and downs. Although, there's one particular scene between the two that I cannot disclose, but found a little questionable and wonder if it is really necessary. All I can say is it could have been written differently and at another part of the book. The best characters in this entire series, however, are Tharion and Ithan. Tharion 'I wanna be where the people are' Ketos is quite simply a hot mess. In fact, there has never been a hot mess, that was hotter or messier than this sweet himbo. He makes one bad decision after the other and drags everyone he loves down with him. I'm sorry to say this but it's hilarious. The boy is the living embodiment of "Your life's so sad, it's funny" and I mean this in the nicest way possible. He needs a hug and a really good therapist. Nevertheless, he gets some of his shit together eventually, but there's still plenty of room to grow. Then, there's Ithan 'I want to help but I am super bad at it' Holstrom. As the nickname suggests, he desperately wants to help his friends, the wolves, and the whole world. The problem is that he can't quite manage to do that very well. The sentiment is there, but that's as much as he has going on for him. It's usually not even his fault, it's just that the pup is simply out of luck. At least for the majority of the book. He comes around eventually. A little bit. No wonder he's such good friends with Tharion, amiright? The good news is that since their respective stories and characters are still in need of development in all aspects, I have a feeling that the next Crescent City books SJM has mentioned will revolve heavily around them 🤞🏻 We'll see what we see, though. Finally, I couldn't possibly not mention the most delightful part of the story. At the end of HOSAB, Bryce uses The Horn and ends up in Velaris. Now, I truly loved every minute of this plotline. I squealed like a little girl just at the sight of the names on the paper. I swear I actually did. If I had one little complaint, it would be that I expected a lot more presence from the Inner Circle. I would have loved it more if the gang had been more involved in the story and that more of them would be there. I was expecting an epic Avengers: Endgame style showdown, which happened in a way, but not exactly in the way I had hoped. It did not diminish the experience in the slightest, however. If anything, I'm still dying to read the next book in the series, whenever that comes out.

RATING BREAKDOWN Characters: 4⭐️ Setting: 4⭐️ Plot: 3⭐️ Themes: 2⭐️ Emotional Impact: 2⭐️ Personal Enjoyment: 3⭐️ Total Rounded Average: 3 ⭐️ The book picks up where the cliffhanger left us in HoSaB, and Part 1 did not disappoint in that regard. I wanted a crossover to pay off! I needed the clues and easter eggs to be addressed and to lead somewhere. Bryce's point of view DELIVERED in that regard, and that was so satisfying! The other points of view felt a little more drawn out and superfluous to me in Part 1. It felt like they had to somehow match Bryce's pacing, so characters could align for Part 2, and because of that, I wasn't as invested and got frustrated with what felt like filler. I am so invested in Ithan and Lidia from the previous books, but the pacing in Part 1 disconnected me from them. The mini climax between Parts 1 and 2 was top-tier SJM writing! As Bryce is getting reveals upon reveals, Ithan is fighting for his life, and Lidia heads up an epic car chase escape. It was fabulous! Absolutely LOVED it. The rest of Part 2 got rough and slow again, but also gave me some ick and cringe, which is so rare for me with SJM. I just got a vibe from so many of the characters (specifically characters in power) that everyone was going through pubescent angst for no reason. It felt like every confrontation led to some leader being bratty and abusive with no substantial motive. It got trite and annoying. And then the main characters would either react by feeling debilitatingly guilty, or sassy AF. At one point, I was truly wondering where all the grown-ups were. Why was everyone reduced to their most juvenile tendencies? To be fair, Bryce has always been a challenging FMC for me in this regard. She's hella capable and powerful, but she doesn't feel mature to me personally. Part 3 got mostly back on track, and we got more crossover delivery which was, again, so satisfying. We also got connective romantic moments that are classic to SJM books. The finale was creative, satisfying, well-paced, emotionally stirring, and pretty perfect. All in all, she stuck the landing. There's dead weight in here though, and that affects my rating. To get specific, I think Ithan's arc with the Fendyr heir could have been cut, and the HoSaB reveal felt a little cheap because of it. I also think Ariadne and Tharion could have been given those pages. Their stories and arcs feel incomplete to me somehow. Despite this, I have good feelings about this trilogy. I look at it as a novella for ACOTAR, and a fascinating and lovable one at that...I just wish it was as punchy as a novella, with some of the excess fat trimmed.

"Two angels ... and a Fae prince ... walk into ... a dungeon ..." If the joke was not a clear sign of incoming spoilers then here's your disclaimer: THIS REVIEW WILL BE FULL OF SPOILERS. So if you don't want to see any, please leave 🏃🏻‍♀️👋🏻 Okay? Okay. The most important thing to take into account for this review: SJM for me is a 5 stars book author, this review does not mean I consider HOFAS a bad book, it was good, great at times, but it did not meet my expectations. Which SJM has meet multiple times before! So, clearing that up, LET'S JUMP RIGHT INTO THIS B. ACOTAR x CC I was really curious and nervous about how this crossover was going to be tackled, in the end, this is a CC book NOT an ACOTAR book. And well, mother delivered. This was FABULOUS. I loved how the crossover did not overpower the CC storyline, they truly complimented each other, this played out exactly how I imagined all the acotar characters would react. It's so weird to think I know fictional characters well enough to know/expect a certain reaction from them. So many theories were proven correct, a great setting was left for acotar 5 and ugh just, round of applause. Perfect. Nesta, I really thought I could not be more obsessed with Nesta and this book proved me wrong. There are so many facets to her character, and seeing the Valkyrie warrior Nesta in action ugh, amazing, then Mommy issues Nesta, wonderful, Lady death Nesta, chills. Too good. Azriel, the shadowsinger spoke more in this small crossover than all the acotar books together lol. I loved getting a better glimpse of what will hopefully happen with Azriel in the next acotar book. Seeing his spymaster side in action, sheesh, I get it Elain, I really do 😮‍💨. Nesta + Azriel, the duo I knew I needed did not disappoint. Their dynamic was so good, during the fight scenes they are so in sync, I was giggling and screaming so much. We also get to see their friend/siblings dynamic, I was crying with Azriel getting Nesta out of the Mask. "Cassian's waiting for you, Nesta," Azriel said– tone gentling. "Take off the Mask." ... "He's waiting for you at House of Wind," Azriel went on. "At home." I need see more of them in the next acotar book. Rhys, I mean there is no way I can dislike Rhys like EVER, loml, but, I'll admit, after ACOSF, I questioned a bit his decisions. But this CC3 High Lord Rhys? OH MY GOD, YES. This was everything I expected from him and more. The power and authority radiated from his character in this book was perfect. I have no other comments. Truth-Teller, I have so many questions, how did Azriel get it? what are its true powers? Is Azriel related to the first high lord of Prythian? I'm confused. Illyrians are MADE, still processing. ACOTAR x CC Bonus chapters, I am a bit tired of the Nesta/Rhys rivalry, I really though we moved past this with ACOSF. I understand both sides I guess, I wouldn't necessarily say, Rhys or Nesta are wrong, both are right? I really hope we can see some type of friendship from them in the future. Also, I would sell my kidney for more Nesta x Ember interactions. CC Moving past the crossover, let's jump into CC, because OH DO I HAVE COMMENTS. Let's start with was pissed me off the most: "Hail Bryce, Queen of the Midgardian Fae." Bryce, um, yeah was not expecting this character 'development'. CC3 Bryce was painfully annoying. In the beginning I really tried to understand her because she was being an ass in Prythian. I thought, I mean yeah she's trying to save Hunt and Ruhn so she'll be reckless, which oh she was. Releasing a f asteri in another world when you don't even know how to kill them?! tf. But okay, then she went back to Midgard and I thought, should be fine now. But NO, she had to be an ass to Hunt too. This made the reading kind of bittersweet because before CC3 I really loved Bryce, she was one of my favorite characters in the whole massverse and now I'm not sure how I feel. Then, we have Bryce dying, which ugh I SWEAR... I don't even want to say much on this, using this plot again was so disappointing. But... Well... Still reeling. Hunt, ugh my baby SON OF HEL, Just Hunt. The trauma this man has had to endure. We finally got to understand where does Hunt come from, Hel. I got a bit confused with the explanation ngl, but I liked it. Quinlar, I'm disappointed. What was that reunion? I expected f fireworks when Bryce and Hunt met again, their interaction at times was kind of awkward and painful to read. If we had not had that bonus chapter I really would be taking of another star from this review because even though this book was more plot focused than romance, Quinlar was straight off its axis. This is literally the only quote from them I highlighted: I'm with you. All of me. You and I, we'll finish this. Ruhn, RUHN DAANAN CROWN PRINCE OF THE VALBARAN FAE (no more) THE MAN YOU ARE!!! I have no comments just quotes, enjoy them: "Lidia," he said roughly, "Finding out who you are... it fucked with my head. To know you're the Hind, but also Lidia– also Day. My Day. But now..." He swallowed. "Now?" Her gaze dipped to his mouth. ... "Now I don't fucking care who you are, so long as you're mine." Her eyes shot to his, again full of surprise. "Because I'm yours Day. I'm fucking yours." I always assumed the Oracle's prophecy meant that I would die. He let his kernel of starlight flicker down the blade, an answer to Bryce's beckoning blaze. One last time. But I am going to live, he said to this father. And I am going to live well–without you. I love you. I fell in love with you in the depths of my soul, and it's my soul that will find yours again in the next life. Lidia, LIDIA IS RELATED TO AELIN OR DORIAN, they way I screamed!!! DESCENDANT OF BRANNON OMFGGGGG, I am sad though because this confirms that TOG is in another timeline no? So no crossover is possible idk but reading this, UNHINGED 😭. I was so excited to learn more about Lidia and this book did not disappoint, the Hind in all its glory. Lidia x Ruhn, THE SHOW STEALERS, the tension, the banter, the angst, STELLAR. Ithan, I read some reviews that mention that Ithan's plotline was boring, well it had me SOBBING ❤️‍🩹, playing the dead proud older brother card had me crying like a baby, his character growth was beautiful. MY PRIME. And as his howl finished echoing, he could have sworn he heard a male wolf's cry float up from the Bone Quarter itself. Specific CC highlights - Ruhn, Declan and Flynn, this friendship is so wholesome. - Jesiba, great closure to her character!! I loved discovering more about her, (before her death lol.) - SABINE'S DEATH - No more of Danika's secrets!!! - Baxian - Rowan's ring cameo confirmed 💍🦅 - The Underking, what do you mean he was called WYRD in another world?! PlEASE EXPLAIN. Specific CC things I did not like / question - Tharion, wtf was going through his mind all of this book?!?!?!?!?! - The final? battle, so much buildup for the Asteri and their downfall was so easy. - The water parasite, kind of random ngl. - The magic language beans 🫘 , again kind of random. - What happened with Ariadne? - What happened with the Viper Queen? - What happened with Sathia? - What will happen with the witches now that Hypaxia is head of HOFAS? - What will happen with the wolfs? If you made it this far into my verbal vomit, thank you 🥹. Mostly everything was wrapped up nicely enough that I am not sure what will happen in the next CC book, because as far as I now there will be another one? Nevertheless, as always, this was an amazing read, it does not get 5 stars because the few things I did not like really bothered me but, I love this world and its characters, here's to god know how many more years till we get more content... LET'S LIGHT IT UP. BYE ❤️‍🔥

SJM’s writing will always feel like home to me! Her talent to weave stories together is unmatched. I can always trust her to pull everything together by the end of a book, although there were a few things I felt were left unanswered at the end of this book. The way she pulls characters together who love unconditionally for each other will get me every time. Through all, love is possible 🫶🏻 Part one, I was smiling and giddy like an idiot. Part two had me falling asleep. Part 3 had me crying and my heart racing. I had to keep reminding myself that this is indeed a Crescent City book and to check my wants/expectations at the door. I’m not rating this book 4 stars because there wasn’t enough of certain characters (IYKYK) - I was pleasantly satisfied with that portion of this book. There were so many epic/incredible moments in this book, but when there’s a solid 150 pages that didn’t captivate me I can’t rate it 5 stars! I’m gonna say it, Crescent City is my least favorite SJM series. While I still love the characters and story, I just feel more emotionally attached to the ones in her other series. This book is my favorite in the series, though! It’s by far and away still in my top fantasy series, and I still really really enjoyed it. I’m a little depressed finishing it! SPOILERS BELOW . . . . . . . . . . . . . I’ll keep this fairly brief, because we did record a podcast episode where we liveish reacted to the parts of the book! Watch everyone become a Nesta fan after this book. I ATE UP every scene her and Azriel were in, and we finally get to hear our man speak more than one word🥰 Lidia and Ruhn were such shining stars for me in this book. The end battle felt extremely anticlimactic to me. Was it emotional at times? Yes. But my heart was racing more when Lidia broke the three amigos of the dungeons. I know SJM loves her characters, but it’s time for her to kill someone lol I truly wish that SJM would have taken the last chapter where Bryce actually meets the Inner Circle in CC2 and put it at the beginning of this book. Everything was wrapped up fairly nicely in this book - minus a few loose ends. I do believe SJM has said Bryce’s story is over, so I’m not entirely sure how the next book will go? Tharion and Ithan I’m assuming? TOG BREADCRUMBS (so spoilers if you haven’t read TOG) . . . . . Lidia being a part of the Brannon line? Lol no wonder I love her so much. I sobbed and had full body chills Urd = wyrd & obviously the under king is from TOG’s world I’m convinced the tattoo on Bryce’s back is wyrdmarks. Ithan wielding ice?? Sooo is he related to Dorian? All of the shifters coming from TOG’s world?? LFG

First of all I need to say that before I wrote this review, I slept on it, I meditated and took several deep breaths. WHAT THE ACTUAL FUCK? I believe this book is an insult to us readers and fans of previous series by this author, let me explain: there is nothing good about the fmc besides her looks which the author makes sure we get to read a description every now and then, portraying being “thick” like if it was a “condition” to either get glorified or victimized. We are more than looks. I get what she was trying with Bryce “joking irreverent” actitud but it got out control, she became a spoiled brat child like with not respect whatsoever for anybody, not even her fucking mate and that is probably the worst. On top of that she is the perfect Mary Sue, there is nothing she can’t accomplish, without a day of training or learning process she knows how to manipulate every single weapon/power/ability and don’t get me started with the powers up, at some point I thought even Rhys himself will appear and give her his own powers and court rights just for the sake of the plot and Bryce superiority to everything. It’s the most flat and empty fmc I’ve ever read and I know it was intended to empower us and represent us as something else than a “damsel in distress waiting for charming prince to rescue us” but it failed. It’s a character that doesn’t go through a developmental growth or character building process and when she actually does something serious you can’t believe her. I can stay here and write an essay about everything that is wrong with Bryce and I will never finished so I will move along to the book structure. The friends they'd made were what mattered in the end. Not the enemies. Through love, all is possible. After waiting so long for this book, it feels surreal to have finally read it. I'm still processing everything I've read and part of me can't believe I've actually read the book, but I just know I'm going to miss this world 🥺 Sadly, it’s not a 5 star read for me, I had some issues with it, but I loved the book, I had the best time reading it and was hooked from the start. I think this every time I read an SJM book, but Sarah is incredible. I wish I could get a glimpse into her mind because I have no idea how she comes up with all these plots 🤯 Unfortunately, there’s no way I can keep this review spoiler free. There are no major spoilers, I just think reading this may influence your opinion on the book in case you haven’t read it yet. And please don’t read this review if you haven’t read the previous books and are planning on doing it. I'm very happy with the way SJM handled the crossover with ACOTAR. I never wanted a big crossover and I was afraid that the ACOTAR characters would overshadow the CC ones, but thankfully that didn't happen. HOFAS feels like a CC book, albeit a slightly different one, and the way the two stories merged was done very well. It's so interesting to see how the two worlds are connected, and I'm even more excited to read the next Acotar book. We have so much new information and I cannot wait to see how it all plays out 🤭 Having Nesta and Azriel as the main acotar characters to appear made me so happy. Nesta is my girl, I love her so much and she stood out in her scenes. She's a badass, a real warrior, and it's incredible to see how confident she is now, so sure of herself and her abilities 🥹 Azriel was amazing too, I'm so curious to know more about him and I have a feeling the next acotar book will have his POV. It makes so much sense to me! This book started off very fast paced, there was a lot of action and a lot of moments where I felt like I couldn't catch my breath and I couldn't put the book down because I was glued to the pages, eager to find out what was happening. But some parts dragged a bit, there was a lot of info dumping, which is a common thing in the CC books, but some of this information was repeated a lot and it got tiring. Bryce was given all the information and I would have preferred to see her find some things out for herself. I also think there were too many things happening in this book, it got to a point where it was too much and my brain could not take it anymore. It was exhausting. Sarah tried to fit so many plot points into one book and it got messy. I was able to understand everything and I'm excited about what comes next, but there was no need for her to drop so many revelations and plot twists. Also, sometimes the change of POV was so abrupt, she cut them off at weird places and I don't know how to explain it, but it didn't flow seamlessly. Which is weird because I think Sarah thrives on writing multiple POVs. TOG is a perfect example of that. : ̗̀➛ Bryce was insufferable in this book and this is probably the main reason why HOFAS is not a 5 star read for me. I have no idea what happened but she annoyed me so much. I love her and I loved reading her POV in the previous books, but in this one I found myself not wanting to read her chapters. She was so impulsive and reckless, did so many stupid things because she would not stop for a moment to think things through. It made me so angry 🤬 I don't know, it was so hard for me to connect with Bryce. I think Sarah was trying to make her into some version of Aelin, but it felt forced and let's be real, there can never be another Aelin. : ̗̀➛ Hunt, thankfully, didn't feel any different to me. I felt so sorry for him because of everything he had been through and it was clear that he was suffering and carrying around a lot of guilt. But I love that he found a way to deal with his feelings and realised that dwelling on the past was not going to help him. Hunt is an amazing male and I hate that so many people can't see that. ・❥・Bryce and Hunt did nothing for me in this book. Their reunion was so anticlimactic and there was a lot miscommunication between them. Bryce, in my opinion, had a horrible attitude towards Hunt. I mean, Hunt was tortured and it was not the first time for him, she was well aware of his past, and still demanded that he be fully involved in her plans to destroy everything and everyone in her path? When she knew he had done something similar in the past and it hadn't gone well? I still love them, of course, I think their relationship is so sweet and I adore their friendship, but I expected more emotional depth in their romance. : ̗̀➛ Ruhn, my love, my life, my baby. He's my favourite male character in the series, I just think he's had a fantastic development, he's grown and learned so much. Ruhn could have been a terrible person, but he rebelled against everything his father wanted him to be and tried to be the best version of himself he could be. I admire how much he loves his friends and family and is willing to do anything to protect them. : ̗̀➛ Lidia is phenomenal, I knew she was going to be my favourite female character in the series and I wasn't wrong. She is the type of character I love, so complex and with so much depth. It was so good to get to know her and see who she really is, not the persona she presents to the world. She has a huge heart, it was very touching to find out everything she did to protect something that was so precious to her. ・❥・ Lidia and Ruhn stole the show, they made their way into my super special list of favourite SJM couples. I loved every scene they were in, they have amazing chemistry, they communicate well with each other and my heart is so full of love for them. Their bonus chapter was the cherry on top for me, so perfect and beautiful. I just wish Sarah had taken more time to develop their relationship, I can't help but feel it was a bit rushed considering we don't have that many scenes with them in the book. : ̗̀➛ Although I didn't hate Tharion and Ithan's POVs in this book, some parts were actually interesting, I have no idea why they had so much focus. Some of their scenes added nothing to the plot and it was just them making stupid decision after stupid decision. But I'm glad that they both seem to have learned something from their past mistakes. Besides my issues with the pacing, the huge amount of information and Bryce's arc, I was also bothered by how easily the villains were defeated. And so many things were just too convenient. And what happened at the end was so predictable, Sarah does that all the time and it's really annoying. I felt nothing when I read that scene. Overall, I think SJM tried too hard with this book, wanted to make it an epic story, but she filled it with too much information and forgot about the emotional depth. Usually Sarah puts a lot of focus on the characters and their arcs, but in this book I felt like the plot was the main character. I expected more, I expected to feel like I was reading a high stakes fantasy, but for some reason I didn’t. I know it seems like I didn't enjoy the book because I pointed out so many issues, but as a huge lover of SJM's books, I can't help but be a little critical because I know what she can do and a part of me wanted a little more from this book 🥲 Still, it was amazing to read this, I really loved it and I love the characters so much. I have no idea what will happen in the next CC book, the main plot is nicely wrapped up but there are some loose ends and I'm curious to see what will come in the next book.

This IB list is full of books doing nothing 2.5 The novel is set in the city of Lviv, Ukraine, and begins with a group of hippies who are meeting at a cemetery for their yearly tribute to Jimi Hendrix. This group includes Alik who works at the theater. This time they are joined by a former KGB member Ryabtsev - who claims to have helped smuggle Hendrix’s hand that is buried in the grave. He fell in love with his music after hearing it so much during his spying on the hippies. On the way home, Alik is almost run over by Taras- who drives people with kidney stones over cobbled streets to help them pass their stones. Every night after being paid he goes to the exchange where Darja works. She’s always locked behind the glass and she’s allergic to money! Taras is neighbors with Yezhi, an old hairdresser, and is friends with Oksana, an actress who also volunteers with the homeless. Most of the book is Taras driving customers around at night and meeting his friends during the day. Or it’s Alik and Ryabtsev chatting and riding a scooter around Lviv. This becomes very circular and repetitive, with not much new happening in any of these events. Something odd is happening in Lviv though- seagulls are attacking people (or Ryabtsev’s birds), starfish are found, and the air smells of sea water. I’m just going to remind you that Lviv is landlocked and closer to the Polish border than the ocean. I guess this is where hijinks ensue? Insert your favorite gang-solves-things show or cartoon reference here. This book is mostly all good vibes and a love letter (or an ad depending on your view) to Lviv. Unfortunately it never rises above this. The stakes never felt very high and the writing is just fine. If you want to read about Ukraine but don’t want to do anything too political (or too exciting), then this is the book for you.

'Jimi Hendrix Live in Lviv' was longlisted for the 2023 International Booker Prize and at first, I remember thinking this seemed like a strange pick for the prize based purely on the title. However (and listen up Jimi Hendrix superfans) this book had quite literally nothing to do with Jimi Hendrix - he was probably briefly mentioned by name about four or five times throughout the duration of 400 pages which I am kind of glad about as I didn't think I'd enjoy some sort of Jimi Hendrix historical fiction/memoir mix. Instead, we are given a magical realism novel that is very reminiscent of Bulgakov's writing who I loved. We follow two plot lines - Taras and Alik whose paths never actually overlap but they show us how they are experiencing a very strange environmental anomaly in different parts of Lviv. The characters themselves were all very likable, if not a little bizarre. I would never have picked this book up on my own accord, had it not been nominated, but this was actually a good book with just all round good vibes.

I went into Jimi Hendrix Live in Lviv by Andrey Kurkov expecting something wild, maybe even chaotic- and in some ways, that’s what I got. Just not always in the way I hoped. The premise is a group of aging hippies gathering around the supposed buried hand of Jimi Hendrix in a Lviv cemetery, while strange, almost supernatural events ripple through the city. It feels like the setup for something profound, or at least delightfully surreal. All in all, the book is enjoyable. Kurkov has this light, playful touch - his characters are eccentric in a way that makes you want to linger with them, and the whole novel has this hazy, slightly absurd energy. There’s humor, oddity, even a kind of warmth in how he portrays the city. Lviv itself ends up being the real heart of the book, lovingly rendered even as increasingly bizarre things unfold. But somewhere along the way, it also feels… a bit off. The plot wanders. There are threads - mysteries, romances, strange phenomena - that never quite come together in a satisfying way. It’s like listening to a bootleg recording that has moments of brilliance but never fully locks into rhythm. Even the Hendrix connection, which sounds so central, turns out to be more of a quirky motif than a driving force. That said, I didn’t dislike it. In fact, I kind of admired its looseness. There’s something refreshing about a novel that refuses to be tightly structured, that leans into atmosphere and character over resolution. It’s playful, a little messy, and very much its own thing - almost like magical realism with a shrug. In the end, I’d call it an enjoyable but uneven read: charming, strange, occasionally frustrating, but memorable in its own offbeat way. Still worth wandering through for the mood alone.
