This Review ✍️ Blog 📖 Twitter 🐦 Instagram 📷 Support me ☕ “Your power is a song, and one I’ve waited a very, very long time to hear, Nesta.” Whenever SJM releases a new book, you start seeing it everywhere related to books, whether it is GR, blogs, book twitter and even memes. I tried to read the book as soon as possible not because I was super excited but because I know some people got zero chills and can’t help but spoiling it for others. And to give you a better idea of Sarah’s success I am gonna provide some numbers here: She sold more than 10 million copies, her books are translated into more than 37 languages, her net worth is around 40 million dollars according to Google and ACOSF, her books that just has been released already has 27K ratings over on GR which takes some books years to reach. I am saying all of the above because I understand that SJM is not perfect and no one said she is. I don’t consider myself a SJM stan and I gave her books all kind of ratings from very bad to excellent according to me! And the important thing is that this is highly subjective, some readers enjoy her books and some don’t which is totally cool. The not cool part is shitting on people who reads her books. The thing is I know this review won’t change much, Sarah will continue releasing books, her readers will continue to read them and the SJW will continue doing their job. I will try to keep this spoiler free and if there are spoilers I will point that out and hide them. But if you have not read the original trilogy then don’t continue this review because you will get spoiled. The story takes place after the events of the last book and it is a full novel focusing on Nesta and Cassian. Nesta is kind of traumatized after the events of the last book and she’s specially affected by her father’s death. She goes into a self destructive cycle which makes Feyre and Rhysand involved to help her. In addition to that there are some issues from the last books that are further explored like the human Queens and the political problems within the different courts. Now here is the thing with SJM stories, I think they have the romance part and the fantasy part. I am a bigger fan of the later part and the first part can sometimes be too cheesy for me! To be honest, this entity is the filthiest and has the most smut in all of SJM books. I think this is not appropriate at all for younger readers. The writing was typical SJM writing, Sarah has the ability to keep you hooked and entertained throughout the story even if it is a 700+ book. There were readers who finished the whole book in one day!!!!! I also believe that Sarah listens to her readers, there was certainly less purring in this one but there were definitely moments that made me cringe. I am not the biggest fan of terms like “Mate, territorial and primal” which are used. Also the character’s ability to smell each other and know who had sex with who always made me cringe and I don’t think it is romantic at all. Another thing I like about the book is the world building, I kind of enjoy the lore and the settings of the world. The magical house in this book was a great addition and I don’t know if it can be considered as a character but I loved it and saw that many readers did too. “She was a wolf who had never learned how to be a wolf, thanks to that cage humans called propriety and society. And like any maltreated animal, she bit anyone who came near.” And speaking of characters, it should be mentioned that this is a character-driven book. I think SJM taker her time to explore characters and trying to expose them to all kind of stuff and also giving us an insight to their backstories so that when the actual plot happens, it is empowered by the reader caring about the character. Nesta grows a lot throughout the book, she starts as someone who is in a dark place, self destructive and cold and we see her slowly becoming a better person through the book. I loved her relationship with Emerie and Gwynn. I tend to like SJM’s platonic love dynamics! However, I thought that Nesta was sometimes not treated fairly and no one acknowledged that fact and they just ganged up against her. Cassian is also good, But I wish Sarah’s males were a bit different and more distinct from one another. Rhysand, Rowan and now Cassian kind of sounds the same with their big wings and bigger cocks. We understand that they have “rippling” muscles and nice tattoos so I wish the author focused on their personalities rather than what we have outside. Az is actually a bit different from them and I want his book right now!!! It is funny how Rhysand was insufferable in this book, and not just to us as readers but also the different characters pointed that out whether by speaking it out loud or rolling their eyes…etc. The plot is there but I feel there were multiple subplots rather than one main plot line. I think after reading 10 of Sarah’s books I became very good at catching her foreshadowing which made almost all those plot lines predictable one way or another. (view spoiler) “Whatever you need to throw at me, I can take it. I won’t break.” Summary: I think it is kind of a typical SJM story that will appeal to fans of ACOMAF. I liked the main characters and I liked their romance but not all the sex and focus on physical traits. I liked some of the sub plots but some of them felt too convenient or predictable for me. It was a gripping read and the last 10% was exciting and addicting. I want the next book to focus on Azriel so can anyone tell me it will be his book please?!

"I've seen what you can do when you are willing to fight for the people you love. Why not apply that same bravery and loyalty to yourself? Don't say you don't deserve it. Everyone deserves happiness. The road there isn't easy. It is long, and hard, and often traveled utterly blind. But you keep going. Because you know the destination will be worthwhile." I truly do not know how to do justice to this book without writing as many words as I can possibly fit into this review. So, this is your warning that this is going to be a lot of words strung together to hopefully make sense by the end. On how moving and special this story is. I will never understand how SJM can put 26 letters together in so many different ways and create such a masterpiece. Such a story. Such a journey. Especially because she only gets craftier and smarter with each and every book she writes. Let's start with "keep reaching out your hand" please. It's not lost on me that the person that tells Cassian to do this is Amren. That even in her own anger and resentment, Amren reminds Cass that sometimes the only thing you can do is continuously be there for someone no matter what they do. It's so beautiful to me that the two people that always encouraged Nesta to be herself are the two people fighting the hardest for her to come into her own. That they're choosing to stand up for her, to fight for her, but also pushing Nesta to fight for herself. When Cass tells Ness that "she can throw whatever she needs to at him because he won't break" and she then says she's not like everyone else and he says "that's never bothered me" it just about makes my heart burst open. It's the first moment she chooses to share something of herself with him, and he chooses to share his past that he's still working through. I love that she sees, for the first time, that working through trauma isn't a straight line, that there are good and bad days. And while she's not even close to being ready to accept it, that scene is so important because it's the first time she sees it. And not only does she see it, but she sees it on someone she respects. Amren had broken Nesta's pride. So she wouldn't have dreamt of hearing it from her. And Nesta believes her sisters have betrayed her by condemning her to the House of Wind. It takes her a long while to realize that what her sisters did by sending her to train and work was to help. That it was out of love. I've seen a so many people say that nobody gave Nesta enough time, that they Pushed her to get better. But that's just not the truth when it comes to a journey with the mind. Sometimes there isn't any drive to get better, and an ultimatum is the only way for someone to get a true start on it. Nesta needed a push, and she got it, and without that push, we never would have gotten to see one of the most beautiful character arcs in history. So let's go into it. The first moment I teared up in Silver Flames was when Cassian got called to the library to get Nesta to stop training in the shelves. That what she was doing was troubling the others and disrupting work. It's such a beautiful moment when Cass first corrects her, then asks her to stop, only to realize that she was doing something she excelled at incorrectly so that all of the females around her would see that he would never do something she didn't agree to in the first place. She makes sure all of the other priestesses see that if there is a male out there that will respect every wish you have, it will be Cassian. Not only do we see her first breakthrough in her broken soul, but we see the first time she acknowledges that Cassian is worth so much more than he believes. It's beautiful, and will always be one of the most special moments I will ever read in a book. When Gwyn's name shows up on the sign up sheet... I can't even begin to explain the jolt of energy that ran through me. That still runs through me. It's so incredibly powerful to see women take their pain and turn it into a controlled rage. It's a protection of the heart, and a drive to make sure that no one can ever hurt them the way they were hurt before. The priestesses are my heroes. And no matter how many times I read this book I will never be more proud than I am of these females. For taking a step and never backing down from what comes of it. Fast forward to Nesta training with a wooden sword for the first time with Cassian with the mantra "never again" repeating as she goes. When she stops and he's staring at her with so much pride in his eyes. When the priestesses around her are staring with awe. And not afraid, but ready to follow her lead. This is so important for Nesta, such a big part of her arc, because all her life she's believed she's let people down. That she's never been worthy. Of course, she still believes that as soon as they find out what she did, they'll only scorn her like everyone else... but she sees, too, that what she's doing is making a difference. And an important one. And it's just another step in the right direction. Not to skip over a huge plot point, I wanted to add that while this book is very sex heavy, it's meant to be. We know from the first moment we meet Cassian that being physical is a huge part of how he let's off steam and deals with his pain. I think it was only inevitable that Nesta would be the same given how similar they are from the very first moment they met. It makes so much sense that their relationship evolves in the same way their sex does. That their story focuses in on the kind of sex they're having. Their chemistry is out of this world, which is why it's so important to see that despite their lack of control outside of training, there is so much respect inside of training that it rarely finds a place in that part of their day. For three hours every day, they let that pass, and Cass still helps her to work out what she needs to in a regimented training. It may have started out as an order, but at some point, it did become a way of Nesta coping, and Cassian offers her that solace as much as she offers him the same. It's a symmetry I think so many people overlook in saying that this book either has too much sex or use the huge amounts of it so say that the message of perseverance is lost in porn. It's only added to with it. And that brings me to chapter 50, one of the most important things ever written. There is a breaking point in all of us, and I remember thinking along with Cassian, that's Nesta's had to be a storm of rage. That the only way she would move out of hate and into love was to yell, and scream, and get it all out in a verbal spew of self-desecration. So when she fell to her knees and cried. I swear I've never gotten through it without crying myself. My quote above comes from chapter 50, because it's just the truth. She does so much for those priestesses up to this point, for Gwyn and Emerie. For her sisters in the war. For Cassian. I will always believe that as soon as she realized she did good in between all of her bad, that's when she finally got over her hump. Sometimes you just have to show your absolute worst, and be your absolute worst, in order to realize that means you have a best too. Nesta was a big part of me realizing that. And while I don't relate to her on every level, she's one of those characters that I'll always hold so close to my heart. Because her broken pieces might not match up to mine, but she fought like hell to put them back together and so did I. So do I. chapter 50 is so special to me. "Nesta began." When she finally makes it down the 10,000 steps without hate being the fuel, it's so beautiful. Because that was when she realized the most important part of a journey such as this. Something that Amren points out to her after one of the most beautiful and true apologies ever written. Darkness can only be dark as long as we don't acknowledge it, and the House being a metaphor for that is just... iconic. And Nesta seeing that acknowledgement and allowing it to wash over her... "I am the rock against which the surf crashes." I don't want to go too much further into the plot simply because I'm not a spoiler kinda girl. And so much of the rest of Nesta's journey is surrounded by the events that happen around her. So I'm just going to share some favorite moments for those that have read it, and hopefully have people who haven't read it come back and enjoy them for all the same reasons I do after they've given it a chance (or a second one, because this book is so special). Gwyn's Valkyrie breathing exercise has been written out in my notes since I first read it in March of 2021. It works. It helps. It's amazing. Gwyn saying "our stories are worth telling" after offering Nesta and Emerie a new manuscript she's helping Merrill write about the rebirth of the Valkyries. The friendship Azriel and Ness make. If I hadn't already been head over heels in love with the male, as soon as he gets her a book light for the dark, I would have been a goner. Fortunately, I already had been a goner, so it just made me love him so much more. The friendship bracelets. "We win to prove to ourselves that it can be done." Ataraxia. Through her own persistence to be stronger and better and never fail another person again, she achieves this. And I think it's one of the most powerful things ever put in a book. Especially because it's a word nobody would have known the meaning of until SJM told us. So powerful. Rhys falling to his knees. Every time. And finally, "I give it all back." This is another controversial topic that I feel as though I want to add my opinion to. You see, this moment is so incredibly powerful because of the choice. Every other thing in this new life wasn't something Nesta got to choose. I think that the beauty of Nesta's character arc is that the first thing she chose to give up everything for was the first person who gave up everything for her. That she was able to give that all back. It's when she let's go of all of that anger and pain and sorrow and regret and makes up for every last bit of it. It only goes to show that sometimes one decision is all it takes to change your life. I just think that there couldn't have been a more perfect way to wrap up Nesta's story. So I hope that if you have a mountain to climb right now, you know that even though you're meant to work through it on your own, you'll always have someone walking the path with you. You'll always have people in your corner, people who want to help you and be there for you. Sometimes it's in the form of pushing you to start a journey that feels too big and too long to take. Sometimes it's continuously lending a hand. Sometimes it's letting someone new in. But most of the time, it's realizing that the only forgiveness that matters in the end is forgiving yourself. That trauma isn't linear and neither is healing. That life is yours to forge, and once you feel everything, let that darkness envelop you, get to the very bottom of who you are... that's when you truly begin. Just like Nesta began. just like Feyre did before her. And just like so many characters, and people, have before them. There's so much more to this story than what I wrote here, and I could probably prattle on forever about it's significance to me, but the beauty of books is that they mean something different to all of us. If you hated this book, I hope this helped you to have a different perspective. If you loved it, I hope you saw a bit of your own thoughts in this. If you were pretty neutral on it, maybe you're thinking of giving it a second chance, or maybe you've finally tipped over the edge on hating it. Whatever the case may be, however you feel, I hope you have a book that makes you feel as incredibly seen as this book allows me to feel every time I open it up. I can't wait to open it 100 more times. 1,000. 10,000. Just like all of those stairs.

Holy cheese balls, this was some wild ride. There were a lot of polarizing scenes. I mostly loved it, but the things I didn’t, I hated them. I’m going to start with the bad, because I need to vent. - (Spoilers below) - I actually hated Rhysand in this book. Absolutely loathe him. All his choices were wrong, all his reasons were wrong. He lied to his mate about her own body. Her baby. He had no right to do something like that. Not only that, he forbade everyone from telling her. And everyone agreed without question. Wtf? And then we are supposed to accept Nesta is the bad one for being honest? Fuck Rhysand, he even had the nerve to order Cassian to take Nesta away from his territory before he killed her. Just the way Rhys hated Nesta in general pissed me off. His ill intended remarks about Nesta were even more infuriating when he decided to use her to find the magical objects and test her own magical swords. Rhysand telling Nesta she always has a choice is fucking rich of him when they had sent Nesta away against her will, evicted her from her home and tore down the whole block of apartments (to hell with the other tenants, I suppose). He didn’t grovel enough to Nesta by the end of the book. It was nowhere near satisfying. And the way he thought showering her with presents and materialistic shit only showed his own privilege and how out of touch with reality Rhys functions. He and Feyre were a bad caricature of who they used to be. It’s sad and frustrating. SJM just ruined them for me. I won’t be able to re-read ACOMAF for a long time, if ever again. And it was one of my favorite books of all times. So yeah, I’m angry. And worst of all, in this book Rhysand became what Feyre ran away from in ACOMAF; Someone overly protective that witholds vital information for her own good. Make it make sense, please. Same can be said about Amren and her attitude towards Nesta. Who does she think she is to suggest not telling Nesta she had forged three magical swords? Honestly, I’d rather Amren had “died” by the end of the third book than seeing her acting like this. The audacity to suggest Rhysand should colonize the other Courts and become High King of everyone. History is full of white men “conquering” other countries full of brown and black people, there’s a name for that, dear Rhisie. Did Amren go completely mad to suggest some of these Courts would willingly and happily give their home away because apparently it’s Rhysand’s birthright? The audacity to think these Courts would give away their identity and freedom because Rhysand deserves it. I’m still baffled. I’m angry Nesta felt like she had to apologize to these assholes and no one apologized to her in return. I’m angry they didn’t support her and made her feel worse, and yet somehow she ended up grateful to them. When she went down on her knee and bowed in front of Amren, I wanted to throw my book against a wall. Rhys, Feyre, Elain, Amren... they all belittled and mistreated Nesta when she was depressed and nearly suicidal. They left her alone for months and one day, they decided they'd had enough and shipped her off to be dealt by someone else. I’m still reeling at Feyre being worried about what people might think of them because of Nesta’s behavior. Some sisterly love. I love how Nesta said no one shipped Elain off when she was catatonic. The double standard was so blatantly obvious. Nesta made them uncomfortable and that’s why they wanted to remove her, not because they were worried, but for selfish reasons. Elain was perhaps the biggest disappointment simply because I didn’t see it coming. The first time her sister needed her, Elain decided to ignore her. Nesta fought for her to the very end, to the point of breaking herself in the process and Elain couldn’t be bothered to even try when Nesta was at her lowest. And they didn’t even have a conversation to fix things up. But being fair, Elain is in a very toxic and unfair situation herself, too. No one is asking her what she wants (which from that bonus chapter, it's obviously Azriel). They are just waiting for her to finally accept the mating bond with Lucien, so they can avoid conflict with the Autumn and Spring Courts. Her own family has taken her voice and own agency away from her. And she has allowed it perhaps believing there isn't other option. But the moment sweet, quiet Elain says "enough", Cauldron help them all. The horrendous slut shaming Amren, Elain and Rhys threw at Nesta was disgusting. Especially Elain, because there’s nothing I hate more than hypocrites. Apparently she cares about waiting until marriage but she actually had sex with her human fiancé. And somehow she ignored that part while she slut shamed her sister for sleeping around. And then Amren confirmed you can be one of the oldest beings still alive and be a bigot. Good for you Amren, here’s your “you’re disgusting” pin. Azriel became the biggest mystery in the book, but his bonus chapter left me with a bittersweet feeling. Don’t get me wrong. It was great to finally be in that filthy mind (SJM didn’t joke when she said he’s a freak in bed) but the way he talked about Elain, like he was entitled to her–because in his mind it’s three sisters for three brothers–like she wasn’t a human being and just an object he deserved. I hate Lucien for his possessiveness over someone who doesn’t even want to be in the same room as him but at least his excuse is the mating bond. What excuse does Azriel have? And then Rhys had to go and remind us how awful he is. The way he spoke to Azriel was unforgiving. Your brother is suffering and you threaten him?? And when he suggested Azriel paid for sex, I hate it when fantasy books normalize prostitution. Hated that remark so, so much. I’m still seeing red just thinking of Rhysand in this book. After reflecting on Azriel, I believe his trauma is preventing him from creating real connections. That’s why he spent 500 years pinning after Mor, even when he knew it was never going to happen. And when he managed to get over her, it was to fall for another unattainable woman. I think deep down he wants Elain because he knows he can’t have her, and that means keeping everyone at a safe distance. And his entitled over Elain is just his insecurity and self loathing manifesting in that twisted way. I used to ship Azriel and Elain so much, and now I hope it doesn’t happen. I can see Gwyn is going to be his mate and he’s going to be so blind by his entitlement over Elain, that he won’t even see it. And I know I’m going to hate that. Thank you SJM for ruining another Illyrian for me. Speaking of Illyrians. Fuck those mysogynistic pricks. They can all rot in hell for all I care. As of right now, I don’t care about the Night Court, The Court of Dreams (snort), Velaries or the Illyrians. They have all let me down and acted in horrendous ways. I’m only interested in the Valkyries from now on. SJM has gone mad if she believes there’s a pass for all this bullshit. I’m actually mad as hell that I can see the influence of JR Ward all over her writing style because it’s obviously suffering from it. But there’s a reason why I gave this book a high rating and here is why: Nesta Archeron, aka Queen of Queens, was everything I had hoped for and more. Being in her head felt so liberating after so many books in Feyre’s. Suddenly characters were acting “different”, being more honest and thus more horrendous, there were cursing and not that annoying “vulgar gesture” nonsense anymore. You can tell how unreliable Feyre was as narrator. And how much more real and human Nesta is than her sister. Nesta’s journey to healing was arduous, the story didn’t take short cuts, we were there with her in every step of the way. There were good days, there were bad days. The symbolism of the 10.000 steps paralleling her own personal journey was amazing. Nesta truly earned her happiness with teeth and sweat and tears. It felt very satisfying to see her climb that fucking mountain and conquer her life back. Nesta’s breakdown felt cathartic and liberating. I broke along with her, feeling everything she was finally allowing to get out. I was there with her, marveling at the emotional level this book was taking me to. Even though I hated the trek to that lake, with Cassian so uncharacteristically cold and unfeeling towards a broken and suicidal Nesta. He could’ve told her Feyre wasn’t mad at her, instead he chose to let her believe the worse and fester in her own agony. Cassian is not like that in any other moment of the story. It felt contrived and a weak plotdevice to “force” Nesta to the breaking point. The way the story centers around mental health issues and abuse survivors moved me to tears on several occasions. Learning to be vulnerable enough to open up to others, even though their reaction terrifies you, learning to love yourself, even the darkest parts, and accepting your past mistakes and forgiving yourself were the pillars in Nesta’s journey. Nesta is just the most relatable character out there. From reading romance books, her new female friendships, the way she fantasized about two hot men and how she expressed her sexuality. The way she hated and doubted herself at every step. We have all been there. I felt like I was Nesta while reading. Just in this book, Nesta retrieved several millennia-lost magical objects, used them without losing herself, created new magical objects with her bare hands, killed the worst thing trapped in the prison, became a Valkyrie, killed the cursed queen, found her chosen family, helped other women with their trauma and circumstances, mastered 10.000 steps and climbed an impossible mountain, winning the Blood Rite, seduced a man with three dances to the point of receiving a marriage proposal right there, saved the life of her sister, brother-in-law and newborn nephew, sacrificing most of her powers in the process, found her mate and even created a connection with The Mother. Let that sink in. The nivel of baddassery that Nesta Archeron achieved in this book is unfathomable. I loved how a big part of this book was dedicated to the sorority among women and the way most men disrespected and disregarded them. And how, together, they found the way to grow strong and fight back. My Valkyrie babies will always have a special place in my heart. Give me a whole mammoth of a book about the new Valkyries training and fighting in sisterhood. I want to read about Nesta, Gwyn and Emerie training new female recruits and creating an unit ready to fight against any Big Bad coming their way. My Vakyrie sisters fighting together and winning the Blood Rite gave me an overdose of serotonins. Nesta thinking she had found her chosen family in Emerie and Gwyn made me cry. I’m so happy she found people who loved her unconditionally. That little something with Emerie and Mor made me scream. I want them to have their own book. I want Mor to set things right with everyone and be honest and loving with her wife (mate???). I’m imagining Emerie in the middle of the Inner Circle dynamics and I’m loving that. Gwyn felt so special to me from the start. I loved her story, her personality. And more specially, I love the idea of her being Azriel’s mate. I want her to go out there, have a life, and be happy. Imagine her giving some attitude to everyone else in the IC. These people need her, lbr. Nesta and the House were my favorite thing. it was absolutely delightful and brought a smile on my face. And knowing Nesta created the sentienness of the House out of pure loneliness and need for a friend only made me love them even more. I was so afraid something was going to happen to that house, I was ready to die for them!! I know people love to bash SJM for her sex scenes. But as someone who’s read a lot of smut, I have to admit I consider the sex scenes in this book to be some of the best out there. In terms of realness, even with all the over the top nonsense (such as ginormous penises), their desires and the way they acted felt really genuine. The fact that Nesta participated actively, and openly enjoyed sex was a breath of fresh air compared to all these protagonists who lay back and let the man do all the work. Did anyone else notice how women in romance novels don’t give head or pleasure the man in any way but allowing penetrative sex? It’s tedious, unrealistic and boring. Nesta Archeron was created to break all the contrived ideas about what a female character should be like and I’m here for all of it. Cassian is my new favorite male protagonist in the ACOTAR universe. Not only was he funny and sensible, he actively fought for equality among the Illyrians. He was not afraid to show vulnerability and emotions. He openly cried. Like Nesta said, he’s a good man. He was there for Nesta in all the different ways she needed. He fiercely protected and loved everyone in his life. I feel like apart from Nesta, he’s the character who shined the most. The fact that he secretly took dancing lessons for Nesta made me swoon for real. And I love the idea of a big mating ceremony, so everyone knows they love each other 🥺 Overall, I loved Nesta’s journey. The rest was just noise. Fuck them all. My girl climbed that mountain. —- These are not mine but represent my feelings perfectly:

3.5 Stars ⭐️ Absolutely loved parts of this book Trigger Warnings for A Court of Silver Flames: PTSD, graphic sexual language, abuse, sexual assault, rape, depression, suicidal thoughts, childbirth complications. Pages mentioning sexual assault/rape: 59, 174-175, 365-366, 380-381, 694-695. Most of these are flashbacks or recollections of previous assaults. Page 365-366 is a scene where it is implied rape almost happens but does not. A Court of Silver Flames didn't really feel like an ACOTAR book. Sometimes it read like a 700+ page fanfic, which if you're only here for the Nessian romance, then I'd give it 4-stars. Personally, I fell in love with SJM's amazing world-building and creative plots, and in regards to those things, ACOSF falls flat. BUT before I go into all that, let me share with you some of the things I LOVED: *SPOILERS AHEAD* The Smut. This book is DEFINITELY +18! Let me tell you, as a married, twenty-seven-year-old woman, there were still a few scenes that left me reeling from heat, while others had me uncomfortable with secondhand embarrassment. 😂 There was plenty of sexual tension, fourplay, and graphic sex - honestly, the best faerie porn SJM has written yet. Apparently, there even was supposed to be a threesome scene, and I'm quite happy it was left out. I don't know if ACOTAR fans were ready for it. 😅 Nessian. My love for them is heavily intertwined with the romantic aspect of their relationship, but I did enjoy seeing Cassian support Nesta through her struggles without taking sole charge of her mental health and well-being. Nesta's Healing Arc. This was honestly the best part about ACOSF. In the previous books, we are inclined to dislike Nesta for her nastiness, coldness, and cruelness. However, since ACOSF is half-written in her POV, we finally see the real Nesta. We learn that she is full of pain, fear, guilt, and self-loathing. That her cruelty, drinking, random f*cking, partying and pushing everyone away have all been coping mechanisms for years of PTSD (either from childhood or guilt for her actions/inactions). I went from hating Nesta at the beginning to completely respecting and truly loving her by the end. Her road to healing is long and painful but beautiful as she learns self-love and forgiveness (of others as well as herself). I think a lot of readers, myself included, will find themselves relating to Nesta a lot more than they thought possible. The friendship between Nesta, Gwyn, and Emerie. This story of healing extends to many others in the book, including Gwyn and Emerie. No matter the horrors each has experienced in the past, together, they learn to trust and find strength in one another. Indeed, we don't get to choose our family, but we can choose our friends; and sometimes, they become our real family. Nesta claiming Gwyn and Emerie as her "sisters" reminds me of how Rhys, Cas, and Az see each other as brothers. I love this new girl gang of bad-a$$ females and can't wait to see how they take on the world! Now for the things I didn't like: The unequal focus on multiple plots. In A Court of Silver Flames, it's Nesta's healing arc, Valkyrie training, Cassian and Nesta's romance, Dead Trove / Briallyn / Koschei, and Feyre's pregnancy. While these plots were well written and intertwined at many points throughout the book, the one with the Dread Trove / Briallyn / Koschei seemed to take a back seat when it shouldn't have. This is the main plotline that will drive the series, and you're telling me in over a 750+ page book, SJM didn't write more than 100 pages about it? I know we will get this info in the next books, but we really needed more groundwork in ACOSF because, as of now, the antagonists' role is weak and not very intriguing. Repetitive storylines. There were many similarities between Feyre/Rhys and Nesta/Cassian's mating story. The males always know first, then the female claim they only want sex for sex or fun, then once they find out or discover they are mates, the female leaves the male, only to reunite and accept the bond. While it's not really a bad maneuver, we've already seen it before. Another time this happens is when Feyre and Rhys almost die . . . AGAIN. But I already knew they wouldn't die because of the plot armor (immunity from death due to their essential roles) laid out for them ACOTAR for Feyre and ACOWAR for Rhys. This is twice now that both Feyre and Rhys have basically died and come back to life due to some random, dramatic miracle. Again, this isn't necessarily bad; I just find it boring and not very interesting. Rhys lying to Feyre. Rhys has always been adamant that Feyre has a choice in every decision concerning her life. But Rhys decides not to tell her that giving birth will kill her, and consequently him. In fact, Rhys lies to Feyre (well, ignores her questioning) about it as we learn from the extended chapter edition but tells the Inner Circle. Since when does Rhys hide sh*t from her? You're telling me the male who sent his mate into the Weaver's Cottage and on other dangerous missions is now not being honest because “I can’t bring myself to give her that fear"? She's not some delicate flower. Plus, as the mother, she DESERVES to know! That's BS. So inconsistent with Rhys' character in the previous book. It's just not something he would do. But you know who would??? Tamlin. Rhys effectively pulled a Tamlin. 😡 Nesta, Gwyn, and Emerie surviving/winning the Blood Rite. I loved that these females participated; however, them not only surviving but winning is unrealistic. They're up against Illyrian warriors who have been training for this moment since childbirth, while they've only been training for maybe 3 months? Honestly, that's not enough time to become proficient in survival or combat skills. There's also a moment when Nesta shoots a bow perfectly, and her reasoning is, “My sister taught me. . . a long time ago.” Girl, Feyre took you out to practice one time. You're telling me you're already a pro?? It's just improbable. Overall, A Court of Silver Flames was decent. I truly enjoyed Nesta's healing arc and the romance, but I wish there were more driving the story. Since I'm a huge ACOTAR fan, I will definitely read the next book hoping that the plot thickens and there are some twists and turns along the way. Just for fun, I want to make some predictions for the next book!!! • Az and Gwyn are MATES! I read the bonus chapter from Azriel's perspective, and there's an interaction that has me thinking this. Her breath curled in front of her mouth, and one of his shadows darted out to dance with it before twirling back to him. Like it heard some silent music. She angled her head, hair shining like molten metal. "Do you sing?" He blinked. It wasn't every day that people took him by surprise, but . . . "Why do you ask?" "They call you shadowsinger. Is it because you sing?" "I am a shadowsinger -it's not a title that someone just made up." She shrugged again, irreverently. Az narrowed his eyes, studying her "Do you, though?" she pressed. "Sing?" Azriel couldn't help his soft chuckle. "Yes." Azriel entered the warmth of the stairwell, and as he descended, he could have sworn a faint, beautiful singing followed him. Could have sworn his shadows sang in answer. I think he's hearing her heart sing to him, and his shadows are singing back. 💕 There's also an important moment in Chapter 52, when Gwyn sings during the priestess service. It says, "Gwyn sang, chin high, a faint glow seeming to radiate from her." I think this could mean that Gwyn is a lightsinger in contrast to Azriel being a shadowsinger. She's the light to his shadows. Two sides of the same coin - his other half. 💕 Also, in Chapter 29, Gwyn mentions that her nymph bones are more pliant than ordinary High Fae, meaning she could give birth to an Illyrian baby! Bye, Elain! 👋 • Gwyn is Tamlin's daughter! In Chapter 29, Gwyn says that her mother participated in the Great Rite with a male stranger. Remember, the Great Rite is where the High Lord of Spring Court has to find the Maiden and bed her to generate magic for the land. Her mother never found out who the father was but says that the magic chose him that night. Tamlin has been ruling Spring Court for at least 50 years, so if it was a High Lord, it was him! I definitely think Gwyn being his daughter is the key to Tamlin's redemption arc if SJM decides to give him one. Tamlin literally has no one: no friends, no family, no mate. He's absolutely depressed and spiraling. What he needs and wants is someone to protect and love unconditionally, and what could be better than the arrival of a long-lost daughter? I don't think anyone in the ACOTAR universe wants to see another Tamlin romantic storyline, so I think the only other possibility is to show a different but powerful sort of love - the love of a parent. I think this could be a beautiful story. I'm here for it. • On the other hand, Gwyn could possibly be Lucien's daughter and Helion's granddaughter. While I think the Tamlin theory seems more probably, here are some reasons why she could be Lucien's daughter. I previously mentioned how Gwyn glows when she sings. This could mean she has inherited some of Helion's light powers, same as Feyre. There's also the fact her hair is described as coppery-brown/chestnut, which indicates she is linked to Autumn Court. However, Gwyn does say her grandparents were from Spring AND Autumn Court so she could have easily gotten it from a grandparent versus a parent. My issue with this theory is that if Gwyn is Lucien's daughter and Azriel's mate, this would create such a weird dynamic in regards to Elain. Too weird. So until we get the next book, I'll keep hoping she's Tamlin's daughter. Also, Gwyn says that magic CHOSE her father that night, which sounds a lot like when magic takes over the High Lord of Spring Court to claim the Maiden - not a random High Fae like Lucien. • Emerie and Mor will become lovers. When Mor visits the library, Emerie is with Nesta: She sighed, nodding toward Mor. “I always forget how beautiful she is. “She never comes to Windhaven these days.” Nesta could have sworn pink stole over Emerie’s brown cheeks. It might be nothing, but with SJM, it's always something. • Eris is getting a redemption arc. During their last conversation in ACOSF, Cassian say, “I grew up surrounded by monsters. I’ve spent my existence fighting them. And I see you, Eris. You’re not one of them. Not even close. I think you might even be a good male. . .You’re just too much of a coward to act like one.” We know that Eris hates his cruel father. He has consistently sided with Rhys and the Night Court to fight against the antagonists of the series. Plus, Eris mentioned multiple times that he left Mor wounded at his border for a reason (alluding to the fact it was in her best interest). While he may be a prick, he seems to have good intentions and follows through with them. This quote just confirms that SJM is setting Eris up for a redemption story. • What if Nesta becomes High Queen of Prythian? Okay, I know it's crazy, but at the very end, Cassian thinks that Nesta has some connection—or understanding—with the Mother. She also hears a woman's voice speaking to her throughout the book, which I think is the Mother guiding her. We know she's was (is?) a death-god and can slay immortals. She mastered the Dead Trove. She will most likely lead a new order of Valkyrie. And she probably will end up killing Koschei with Ataraxia. There are also mentions of Cassian being King of Bastards - which using the title 'king' seems like some suspicious foreshadowing. I don't know how it's all connecting, but I think there's a slight chance they could rule Prythian together. • Elain goes evil. This is honestly more wishful thinking than anything, but I think Elain will reject the bond with Lucien, and when Az realizes his mate is Gwyn, she's going to lose it because it'll be the second time someone she loves rejects her due to fae-related things. A few times throughout the book, Rhys and Nesta say they haven't seen the real Elain. That possibly in the future, "we'll see a different side of her emerge" (Extended Feysand Chapter) versus the sweet and innocent character she portrays. She still has the Cauldron's power that hasn't been fully revealed, and this will probably be important in the next few books.

If you would have asked me this question a year or two before when I was new to reading, I would have told no, I would have told same now also that as long I enjoyed a book it doesn't matter but in this book the out of character thing was not enjoyable at all. Now don't think the characters had a full personality change- just a bit but that bit annoyed me a lot. It felt like Sarah J. Maas had 'adjusted' their personality for the story, for her convenience. I would have loved to see the characters as they were and not just characters but I felt she kept adjusting rules and the world of the fae for the storyline changed them, it was something in book one and it was something in this book. Another thing that annoyed me was that the world of A Court of Thorns and Roses was changed. It felt like everything was happening in the modern era, from the first book I was having olden-era vibes but in this book, everything felt modern- especially the language and there was even a mention of 'mail service' It annoyed me! Why was the same thing not continued! The same language?! Where was my favorite 'The Vulgar Gesture'?! Ugh! Another change I noticed in Sarah J. Maas's writing was well I don't know how to explain this but whenever I read her earlier works, it felt like I was living in that world but in this book I only found few instances to feel that. Also, I found few things about Nesta & Cassian to be similar to Feyre & Rhysand or should I say Aelin & Rowan (from Throne of Glass series)? I am confused between the two. Few dialogues exchanged between Cassian & Nesta were way too similar same as Feyre & Rhysand/Aelin & Rowan, even actions/storyline felt similar. This reason is exactly why after a while I stop reading a particular author's books because everything becomes predictable and repetitive. Let's talk about something important... *drumroll* Nesta! I have never liked Nesta, I have hated her not because she was mean or rude or blah blah blah but because of the way she treated Feyre, she loved Elain but hated Feyre- the person who loved them, who worked for them, who could have left them and had a proper life just by earning only for herself, who despite all hatred from Nesta still worked for them! And the reason that was given in this book for all her actions- I am not satisfied with that, I kind of sympathized with her while reading this book, even almost started liking her but keeping in mind all her actions I just found those reasons to be like that of a 'spoiled child' but since she is the reason why I liked Feyre even more in book one and she did some really good things in this book, all I can do is forgive her (cause I am great 😌😌✌). I don't hate her but I also don't like her (just a bit, I guess) Now I want to talk about something that has been eating me alive from A Court of Frost and Starlight and it is the whole situation with Tamlin. I get it what he did was bad, I remember I was b*thing about him *coughs* a lot while reading A Court of Mist and Fury but after A Court of Frost and Starlight I just thought few things *My mother: Finally this girl is using her brain for something* Tamlin was going through same problems as Feyre, yes, what he did to her was completely wrong & it definitely shouldn't be justified but should we forget what he went through? That even he had problems? That even after finding out things between Feyre & Rhysand he still helped them? And by now Rhysand & family should have forgiven him, they all seem like they forgot what Tamlin did for them, they still hate him so much and I mean so much. If Sarah J. Maas wanted to show him negative why not show him negative completely? Why throw positive bits and pieces? And now I feel bad for Tamlin, everybody is acting like he is completely bad that he didn't do anything well, it is pissing me off because now Rhysand & The Family are showing double standards. They like NESTA & even ERIS!, they pity them, understand them but the same is not with Tamlin! Somehow Tamlin is different?! Ugh! (view spoiler) Wow while writing this review I have changed the rating 4 times and reached 3 stars from 4.5, again Ugh! When I first picked up this book I thought the only reason I wouldn't like this book would be because I had higher expectations and then was disappointed but surprisingly it wasn't that. I liked + enjoyed this book despite all the above which were 'thorns' in my side while reading this book hence 3 stars. Now somebody give me more of Azriel please! Please book gods let there be a book for Azriel, Lucien & even Tamlin, or at least give them a happy ending! And don't let the above problems be there in Azriel's book. Buddy read with Snezana A few years back I joked that I'll read anything SJM writes and I'll definitely love it, how wrong I was. I spent a day after reading this thinking whether there is anything I actually love in this book and I can't pick any, I'm either indifferent or outright hate everything about this book. This book is 600+ pages, everything here can fit into a 300+ pages book. This is not an EPIC FANTASY, I repeat this is NOT an EPIC FANTASY, this book is an erotic fantasy with random things thrown into it, in my opinion there is absolutely no plot. This is supposed to be Nesta and Cassian's book but SJM added way too many things about Rhys and Feyre that added nothing to the plot. SJM also did a mistake of tying up all loose ends in ACOWAR, so instead of creating a whole new villain, she picked a Slavic mythology that was badly executed. Another random thing is the Norse Valkyrie that she added here, another horrible execution. This book is also contradicting, remember when we read ACOMAF and we were willing to agree that Tamlin is evil, well that shit is old, instead of finding a better redemption story for Nesta, she made made everyone sort of mean, hypocritical, negligent and unnecessarily violent so that Nesta can come up on top, why the lazy writing. It's like the characters got replaced by body snatches. Absolutely nothing was hard for the characters, they achieved everything and got everything they needed by luck, it was so easy, barely an inconvenience. The writing is what ruined this book for me, if it was better written I would have ignored the other things in this book. The world building didn't help either, it was way too contemporary, they were doing yoga, meditation, abdominal exercises etc. SJM didn't even bother making it better. SJM can't describe moving things, whether from dance scenes to fight scenes, the depiction was horrible. Even the creatures were badly described, here are some example. Fists and feet and wings, punch and block, kick and stomp, breath sawing out of them as he and Az tried to break past each other’s defenses. What is this? The thing that crawled over the ridge had been crafted of nightmares. Part cat, part serpent, all black fur and sharp claws and hooked teeth. “Welcome back to the Night Court, Nesta Archeron.” Nesta’s story was gorgeous and enraging and tear-jerking and sweet and I wouldn’t have had it any other way. There’s no possibility of me being able to write a review without spoilers so don’t read past my spoiler warning if you haven’t finished the book :) Also, this review is not going to be coherent at all because at this point I don’t care about grammar, I just have to get everything out before I forget my thoughts. Warning: MAJOR SPOILERS FROM THIS POINT ON. ⇢Nesta Wow. If you hate Nesta after reading this book then… I honestly don’t know what to say because that seems impossible. I think it goes without saying that I loved Nesta’s journey. (I’m going to try not to refer to it as an arc because I don’t think it was exactly a redemption arc since it was more of a healing or spiritual journey of sorts.) I loved how while Cassian was a part of that journey, so much of it was her alone, as well as her with her own “Inner Circle” comprised of Gwyn and Emerie. I had really hoped that Nesta would find her people in this book, and it certainly delivered on that front. And it was honestly such a good decision for Emerie and Gwyn to heal alongside her because it just made everything feel even more powerful. “A chosen family. Like the one Feyre had found for herself.” And the whole Valkyrie concept was fantastic! I loved how powerful they became not just mentally, but physically, “Tamlin shrank from her outstretched finger, claws digging into the earth. “Put that finger down, you witch.” Nesta smiled. “I’m glad you remember what happened to the last person I pointed at.” She lowered her arm. “We’re going now.” She stepped back to where Cassian was already waiting, arms open. He wrapped them around her waist. Nesta glanced to Eris, who gave her a shallow, approving nod, then vanished. Nesta said to Tamlin before they shot into the skies, “Tell anyone you saw us, High Lord, and I’ll rip your head from your body, too.” I think the only thing that annoyed me about Nesta’s journey was that as much as it was about her growing, I hated that (MOSTLY AT THE BEGINNING) it felt like she owed the Inner Circle something. Like she had to get better for them, to apologize to them. Maybe this is only my perspective because I understand where she was coming from when she made the bad decisions in her life, but I would have liked to see the IC understand that even though she hurt them, they hurt her too and that they had no right to treat her the way they did. She owed them nothing, but the way the book played out earlier on it really seemed like the IC just blamed her for everything which really annoyed me. But we’ll get into my feelings about the IC later. ⇢Nesta and Cassian Okay so I really didn’t know what to expect for them going into this, but I definitely didn’t think that SJM would pull a death trope situation or have them end up with anyone else because that doesn’t seem to be her style. Okay maybe I did have expectations lol. (Also, I just realized that I made it seemed like they died or something- THEY DIDN'T!!) But guesses aside, I really liked their romance. It was definitely not my favourite part of this book, but it was still pretty good and achieved what I wanted going into this novel. Nessian was never going to be my favourite couple in this series so I wasn’t disappointed that I didn’t fall head over heels for their relationship like I did for Feyre and Rhysand’s when I first read ACOMAF. “Cassian smiled at her, and the world faded away. The music was no longer the most beautiful thing in existence. He was. Nesta couldn’t stop it then. The answering smile that bloomed through her at last, stealing across her face, bright as the dawn.” I wasn't going to mention this but I sort of want to talk about it now so I will. THEY WERE MATES. I honestly didn't know if SJM would make them mates because it's supposed to be super rare, but I shouldn't have even considered that she wouldn't because she loves soulmates, doesn't she? I definitely wouldn't have cared if they weren't mates so I also didn't care all that much that they were, so all I want to add to that is that I'm glad that the mating bond didn't play a huge part in their story. I'm glad that while it did play a role, it wasn't as focused upon as in ACOMAF and ACOWAR. ⇢Other Characters This book taught me so much about perspective. Because when you read ACOMAF AND ACOWAR, it’s easy to fall in love with the inner circle, but you forget how skewed your perspective is, reading from the pov of Feyre, who obviously loves Rhysand and all of the others. Now I’m not saying this book made me hate the Inner Circle or anything, but oh my god did my perception of them change. (Mostly Rhysand and Amren but also Feyre and Elain.) Reading from Nesta’s perspective was a breath of fresh air and it was so interesting to see the IC from the point of view of someone who doesn’t hero-worship them like everyone else. Okay, that was all my really nice way of saying that I HATED RHYSAND in this book. OH MY GOD, I WANTED TO MURDER HIM FOR THE FIRST 75% OF IT. By the end of the book that hate had mostly lessened but holy he was unbearable and just way too rage-y for me. Like I get that it was because of the baby (which I will talk about soon) but CALM DOWN SIR. Edit: Now that it's been a while since I read the book, I definitely don't feel the same rage towards Rhys that I did. I still don't understand some of his actions but I no longer want to murder him lol “You are to treat Gwyn with kindness and respect.” ^ You don’t even understand how angry I was at Rhys after he said that.. WHY WERE HIS OPINIONS OF NESTA SO LOW??? But all those rants aside, Mor was gone for a big portion of this book so I hope we see her more in the next one. We also didn’t see that much of Elain (which was surprising considering her relationship with Nesta), but omg the scenes that she did have were ICONIC. “But Elain said, “I went into the Cauldron, too, you know. And it captured me. And yet somehow all you think of is what my trauma did to you.” As promised, onto the Feysand baby, as people have been calling him. I really didn’t want the Feysand baby to be a thing in this book, because you know, LIVE FEYRE!! YOU HAVE HUNDREDS OF YEARS!! WHY DO YOU WANT AN ANNOYING CHILD SO EARLY? But yeah it happened so whatever. ALSO WHY THE NAME NYX. LORD SAVE ME. I MEAN IT’S NOT TERRIBLE BUT IDK it just bothers me. Okay, rant over. Honestly, I liked how the baby played into the storyline even if what happened with Nesta’s powers is one of my least favourite tropes, so I won’t complain too much. I guess I was just disappointed that after all Feyre went through she didn’t end up savouring her freedom for that long. Not that the baby is going to rid her of her freedom but I think you get my point. ⇢The Plot Okay I literally just realized that I totally forgot to talk about the plot oops. So I personally think that ACOTAR is a very character-focused series, so I was quite surprised by how much happened in this book. I mean there were so many mini-plots and conflicts and it was way more than I was expecting. I actually really liked that, but it was definitely a bit harder to follow than the other books so I get why other people weren't a fan. I loved the rite part and the conflict with the Kelpie, and I'm super interested to see what conflicts continue on to the next book! Warning: Spoilers for the Bonus Scenes. ⇢Azriel Bonus Scene OH MY GOD. OH MY GOD. OH MY GOD PLEASE TELL ME THE NEXT BOOK IS NOT GOING TO BE A LOVE TRIANGLE OH MY GOD I ALREADY KNOW IT IS UGHGUGHUGH. *Cries tears of anger* BUT AT LEAST THERE’S A POSSIBILITY FOR ELRIEL? AND NOW AZRIEL x GWYN?? WHAT IS HAPPENING??? Okay now that I got that out, I honestly don’t see Azriel and Gwyn becoming a couple. Not just because I like Elriel because honestly I could see myself liking either of them with someone else, but simply because Gwyn doesn’t seem like someone that SJM would have as a main character, and because I feel like the next MC will be Elain so that all of the sisters get their story written before anyone else like Mor or Vassa. Please let me know what you think if you have an opinion on this, though. Also please note that I am an Elain stan ALL THE WAY. I hate all the Elain slander I've been seeing recently. I really need to reread this bonus scene because the one I read was incomplete and messed up so I didn’t grasp everything fully, so hopefully, I can read it properly soon because IT WAS SO GOOD. ⇢Feysand Bonus Scene Okay, I definitely didn’t like this bonus scene as much as Azriel’s, but it was still nice to see them happy I guess. ** spoiler alert ** okay before i get started, i have to warn you all, this review is absolutely riddled with spoilers. as in, you probably wont get two sentences in without reading a spoiler. and review. the fourth (fifth, if you count acofas) installment of the a court of thorns and roses series by sarah j maas, titled a court of silver flames, follows our main character, nesta as she adjusts to her new fae body and goes on a journey of healing and growth after an awful war. this review will be divided into five parts: characters, plot, romance, writing and miscellaneous. starting off, im going to be discussing my thoughts on the CHARACTERS in this novel. im upset. some of my all time favorite characters in this series were acting so different, literally to a point where it made me hate them. i understand that this book was supposed to be "nesta's perspective", and naturally, that would put the inner circle in a different light, but some of the characters's actions were inexcusable and just plain rude. im going to dive a bit deeper into each individual character and my opinions on them. nesta: previous to reading this book, i was somewhat indifferent about nesta. all around me in the book community, people would be getting into all out arguments about whether nesta was a good character or not, and i was just over here like "azriel. i want azriel book. now. please." but sarah j maas did a great job in converting me to a nesta stan. the way her different coping mechanisms were displayed were wonderful, and nesta's voice in the story was touching, if a bit dramatic. her character arc in general was great, and im glad that shes apologized for her past actions, but has still stayed true to her iconic self. and also, can we talk about the fact that she has a romance novel addiction? i loved that. cassian: i found cassian to be a little annoying in this book.he was simultaniously dry and obnoxious. you can only make so many dirty jokes before someone begins to find you to be irritating. this is very random, but cassian literally made a "your mom" joke at some point in this book. was that supposed to be funny? there was also a point in the book where cassian "punishes" nesta by making her do physical labor and go on a hike to the point where she passes out. this is not okay. never has been. never will be. overall, his character felt contrived and i felt pretty detatched from him. cassian was never my favorite, but i expected to like him a bit more than i did. gwyn: gywn's friendship with nesta, and her story, was so heartwarming. she was such a wholesome character that i look forward to reading more about. and guys, i think sarah has been dropping hints for a gywn x azriel romance, which i would be so down for. also i saw a theory that tamlin is gwyn’s father? that would definitely be interesting. emerie: EMERIE AND MOR?!?!?!? YES PLEASE. azriel: AZ AZ AZ AZ AZ AZ AZ. azriel was by far my favorite part of this book. his dry humor, his self conciousness, his relationship with nesta, his training strategies, his worry for feyre. i didnt have the specific edition, but i read the bonus azriel scene online, and honestly i feel like he was acting very out of character. he gave the necklace he bought for elain to gwyn. which is fair i guess, because i hate elain and i love gwyn, but he was just acting so... cold? im feeling confliucted UGH. THE NEXT BOOK BETTER BE THE AZ BOOK AND IT BETTER BE GOOD. rhys: oh boy, be prepared for a rant. RHYS WAS AWFUL IN THIS BOOK. THAT IS THE BOTTOM LINE. HE TREATED NESTA LIKE CRAP. HE DIDNT EVEN TELL HIS OWN WIFE THAT THE BABY SHE WAS CARRYING WOULD KILL HER?!?!? SO MUCH FOR "FEMINIST". in a court of mist and fury rhys was the loving, understanding companion that one would need after facing awful circumstances and dealing with PTSD. where did this man go? rhys in this book was all like "nesta. you can cope. just please cope in a way thats convenient for me." it infuriated me to no end. feyre: feyre, unlike her mate (*retches*), stayed unproblematic throughout this book. she was continuously nice to nesta, despite the crude actions of her friends. i do wish she had stood up a bit more for nesta, especially against rhys, but in my opinion, she handled nesta's coping best out of the inner circle, besides from azriel. and yes, i was pretty tired of feysand (they already had there time to shine), but i was glad to find out feyre was pregnant and appreciated seeing her display her undying love for nyx (which, by the way is an EPIC name. it literally means night!) amren: was never a huge fan of amren to begin with, but she was insanely rude in this book. was that always a thing? i dont remember that being a thing. eris: i am so interested in eris's story. so cryptic. so mysterious. is he getting a redemption arc?!?! characters that i could talk about, but wont (for various reasons), are elain, lucien, and mor.
