At least, they did when my husband and I got married there 29 years ago! Cheers and enjoy!

** spoiler alert ** “Edge of Honor” by Brad Thor is a great 4th of July thriller. is the 24th Scot Harvath novel, published in July 2025. It is a gripping tale that follows the ex-Navy SEAL and counterterrorism expert, Scot Harvath, as he returns from a six month honeymoon with his new wife, Solvi, to find himself entangled in a DC power grab orchestrated by a shadowy cabal seeking to control America. The novel explores themes of faith, family, and freedom, which resonate deeply with me. Harvath’s resilience is tested as he navigates a series of intense action sequences, from a blistering ambush on Embassy Row to covert operations that keep the reader on the edge of their seat. Harvath’s balanced approach, characterized by his love for Solvi and his team, evokes a sense of family fighting for what is right. Thor’s sharp writing maintains a realistic portrayal of the action, infusing the story with a compelling emotional core. “Edge of Honor” concludes with a resounding bang, embodying Thor’s signature blend of bold patriotism and unwavering loyalty. It leaves the reader feeling proud of American values and eager to delve deeper into the political underbelly of Washington, D.C., as revealed in the subsequent novels in the series. I highly recommend “Edge of Honor” for readers seeking a fast paced, thrilling, and thought provoking read. Its captivating narrative and enduring themes make it a must read for fans of the genre.

In Edge of Honor, Brad Thor plunges readers into a covert operation that’s as morally fraught as it is pulse-pounding. The protagonist—a seasoned Navy SEAL—is tasked with a mission that tests not only his tactical skill but his ability to navigate shifting allegiances and political landmines. Thor wastes no time: the action kicks off early and rarely lets up, with tight chapters that propel the story forward like a well-planned assault. What makes this novel stand out is its focus on the mission itself. The stakes are immediate, the objectives clear, and the obstacles formidable. Whether it’s infiltrating hostile territory or decoding the intentions of supposed allies, the tension is constant and grounded in real-world plausibility. Thor’s attention to operational detail adds authenticity without bogging down the pace. While there are echoes of past regrets, they serve more as fuel than distraction. The heart of the book lies in the choices made under pressure—what honor demands when the rules blur and the cost of failure is measured in lives. A must-read for fans of military thrillers who crave action with consequence. Thor proves once again that he knows how to write missions that matter.

Another solid entry from Brad Thor. Harvath foils a plot on home soil instead of running around abroad, which made for a nice change of pace. I like how Thor always ties things to current events and the political climate. The claims about the president in this one was clearly Trump-inspired, and the book pulls in allusions to radicalized political discourse. The character Caughlin felt like a Tucker Carlson / Alex Jones mash-up, and the presence of far-right extremist groups kept the plot timely and grounded in reality. The “chaos for chaos’s sake” angle of the attacks stuck with me. It raises questions about what real-world events are driven by true motives and what’s just engineered to stir up division, discord and distrust. The plot got a little too convenient in spots, but it was a page-turner and kept me up late. At this point, I feel like the reader gets what they want in the form of cameos from the favorite usual suspects we have seen throughout the novel, but similar to the Entourage movie, it may come at the cost of this not being a 5 star review. How old is Harvath supposed to be at this point anyway?? 55?? Still a badass, and curious what the future holds for one of my favorite characters out there.

This is the 25th book in Thor’s Scot Harvath series (at least by my count!)- and, in my opinion, one of the best! After his last assignment, Harvath has left his job with the Carlton Group and married Solvi, a agent in the Norwegian Intelligence Service, and embarked on a six month honeymoon traveling the world and winding up back in the Washington DC area. And just as quickly as he had stepped back, he is thrust into action by a violent attack at a rally in front of the home of the Vice President of the US. An important NATO summit meeting is to happen a few days later, and Solvi is asked to assist in the protection of her home country’s Prime Minister. When a motorcade carrying the PM and the Norwegian Ambassador is attacked, Scot is back full time in finding out who is behind these attacks - who hopes to gain? This is a non-stop book - each time Harvath uncovers what he thinks will lead him to the ultimate owner of these horrific attacks, he realizes he is just uncovering one page of a large book. This edition in the series is quintessential Harvath - along with many of his associates (especially Nicholas) from earlier books. While one might imagine this is the final chapter in his story - I don’t think (hope!) so. Thor is at the top of his game in this great series.

After the events of the past few books, Scot and Sølvi decide they needed a break. Scot resigned from The Carlton Group, and Sølvi took leave. They spent six months honeymooning around the world. Back in DC for Independence Day celebrations, they get tangled up in an attack on some protesters which, of course, is the tip of the iceberg of a conspiracy to topple the president and shatter the nation. One of Brad Thor’s greatest strengths is his ability to take the pulse of the state of the world. Here, he has taken the deep political divisions that exist in America today and ask some what-ifs. This president does not resemble the current real life president, but the hatred some of the country feels toward him is. What if… other politicians or other nations take advantage of that? What if… podcasters and social media can be manipulated to spread a specific message? What if… disenfranchised men can be convinced to attack innocent people they don’t know just to sow discord and fear? This is a book that will make you think about who the enemy actually is and who might be behind the voices we are listening to. I enjoyed this book and would recommend it to lovers of action thrillers. Not family friendly due to profanity and violence.

"Edge of Honor" by Brad Thor plunges readers into a high-stakes world of political intrigue and global conspiracy, with America's top spy, Scot Harvath, at its center. After a six-month honeymoon abroad with his new wife, Sølvi, Harvath returns to a vastly changed political landscape in the U.S., marked by a new administration and escalating power struggles. His quiet return is shattered by a brazen terrorist attack in Washington D.C. that he and Sølvi narrowly escape, quickly pulling them back into the shadowy world they had momentarily left behind. As the initial attacks escalate and domestic and international threats intertwine, Harvath finds himself navigating a complex web of deceit where trust is fleeting and the very fate of the nation hangs in the balance. The narrative unravels a deep-seated conspiracy involving shadowy elites and potentially even elements within the U.S. government, aiming to bring the country to its knees. With enemies at every turn, including long-standing adversaries like Russia, internal hate groups, and highly trained operatives, Harvath is forced to rely on his unique skills and a newly formed, trusted team to uncover the truth.

** spoiler alert ** In the 24th Scot Harvath thriller, Scot Harvath returns from a six-month honeymoon with his Norwegian wife, Sølvi, to a divided America under a new administration. Planning a quiet Fourth of July, they're thrust into action when gunmen attack protesters outside the vice president's residence, leading to a deadly shootout at the Norwegian Embassy. Harvath, retired from the Carlton Group, protects a former ambassador amid rising unrest over the president's unfulfilled promises. Sølvi guards the Norwegian PM during a NATO summit. Parallel investigations reveal terrorist attacks orchestrated by a cabal of white supremacists, rogue ex-federal agents (FBI, CIA, Secret Service), and Russian intelligence aiming to destabilize the U.S. through disinformation and violence. Harvath teams with the Carlton Group, ex-CIA Chief and FBI agents to uncover betrayals by U.S. officials who want to see the President resign. Harvath saves the day again and he and Solvi enjoy the Independence Day celebration. Another great page turner!

Scot Harvath and his new bride Solvi have just returned from an extended world-wide honeymoon. On the way to an evening out at the Norwegian Embassy, they are passing a peaceful protest in front of the Vice President's resident, when suddenly the protesters come under attack from fully armored men. Thus begins a heart-stopping, mind-blowing series of events that drag Scot back into the Carlton group and counterintelligence while Solve is recruited to help with the Norwegian ambassador. Meanwhile FBI agents Jennifer Fields and Joseph Carolan have been put in a basement office to investigate a special Russian Operation suspected of infiltrating the U.S. government. Eventually, the two lines of investigation come together to discover a plan specifically targeting the administration of the newly elected president. Power hungry politicians, money hungry employees, media manipulated by persons for self-interest, behind the scenes machinations by foreign leaders to divide the country by creating terror with random shootings and destructive activities - gee, it sounds like today!

Brad Thor delivers yet again as Harvath brings the fight home. At first, I have to admit, I felt myself wanting more gritty action. I love the way Thor describes foreign lands, introducing us to worlds most of us, thankfully, will never know. Though not lacking in action, it just felt "different," for lack of a better description. There was no clear-cut villain with a sinister plan to root against. There were no foreign religious or political zealots to loathe. They don't have legions of minions marching in their streets chanting for death to the US and our allies. They don't profess their deep-seated hatred of our way of life. Instead, they claim quite the opposite. That's when the genius of Thor's plot line occurred to me. The villains in Edge of Honor live in the shadows... no name, no face, no soul. They don't have the benefit of shouting their plan from the rooftops. They whisper them in dark corners, because they are one of us.

Scot Harvath and his new wife Solvi have been honeymooning for six months. Upon their return to Washington D.C., they are on their way to the Norwegian embassy when a peaceful protest at the Vice President's residence turns into a massacre, which they are able to thwart. A former military advisor is attacked because the new President has refused him Secret Service protection, and there is a plot to force the President to resign in favor of the Vice President for not delivering on his campaign promises, led by a vengeful Senator and a rogue podcaster. Scot and a couple of friends agree to protect the military advisor, and Solvi has a favor called in to help protect the president of Norway on her visit for a NATO conference. Both Scot and Solvi have to defend their charges from superior numbers and firepower, respectively, causing Nicolas to look into governmental corruption and collusion, using the resources of the Carlton Group. The end game for the cabal is a doozy.

Brad Thor has truly outdone himself with this thrilling novel! Get ready to dive into the action alongside Scott Harvath, an incredible ex-Navy SEAL and intelligence operative, who finds himself caught in a whirlwind of excitement that will keep you on the edge of your seat. From the very first page, the story grabs you tight, making it hard to put down—you won’t want to miss a single twist! As Harvath plunges into a dangerous conspiracy, he faces shifting alliances and high-stakes politics that put everything he stands for to the test. Each turn of the page pulls you deeper into a world filled with suspense and intrigue, as Harvath races against time to uncover a plot that could change everything. This is a must-read adventure that promises to thrill and inspire! Enjoy the journey!is packed with action and intrigue, as Harvath races against time to unravel a plot that could alter the course of history

Scot Harvath returns in Edge of Honor, and the adrenaline kicks in from page one. What begins as a peaceful retirement in the United States, complete with his new bride and plans for a quiet Fourth of July, quickly spirals into chaos. Instead of fireworks, Harvath finds himself in the middle of a gunfight outside the Norwegian embassy. From there, the stakes escalate as he’s drawn into unraveling a conspiracy that threatens to shake the very foundation of the nation. This installment delivers exactly what fans expect: relentless action, sharp pacing, and Harvath doing what he does best. While the plot isn’t groundbreaking, it cleverly weaves in elements of America’s current divisions, adding a layer of relevance without overshadowing the thrill ride. Edge of Honor is a solid addition to the Scot Harvath series. Fast, fun, and packed with the kind of high-octane moments that keep readers turning pages late into the night.

From the beginning with Lions of Lucerne, I have never read a Brad Thor novel that didn’t capture me from the opening pages and keep me riveted all the way through. Edge of Honor continues this trend. In fact, this may be Thor’s best novel in his extensive catalog. As a notable reviewer wrote: “Brad Thor brings the fireworks!”, and he most certainly does from the opening pages. The fast paced action and intrigue persist throughout this page turner centered around the heroic Scot Harvath and his entertaining cast of characters including Solvi, Carolan, Fields and, my personal favorite, Nicholas the Troll. The characters make every Thor novel memorable while the stories and action keep the pages turning. You will NOT be able to put this one down! There is a reason Brad Thor is a Tier One operator among authors!

Another book in the Scot Harvath series, if you haven't read the others you can read this as a stand alone but I like knowing all the background of things that are mentioned in this book. Just like the others this one is believable - in fact a little too believable - it's scary. I had love/hate feelings while reading it. Did I really think this could happen? Yes. Should I put the book down and stop reading so I don't worry about how realistic the theme is. Yes. But did I? No. This book weaves a gripping story of what “could be” going on in our country right now! Domestic terrorism, foreign interference in our country, power, greed…it’s all in there. The other win for me personally is Scot's fictional home is located down the river from where I grew up very easy for me to visualize.

Top flight thriller/adventure. Scot "Norseman" Harvath teams up with Nicholas, Mike Haney and the ex-CIA director to tackle a chaotic DC pair of shootings one of which involved his new wife, Solvi. Who are the bad guys? Americans! Impossible. Worse, they're ex-CIA! Following this twisted trail is demanding and draining, especially for a man who's trying to leave the clandestine service and settle down a bit. Still, the nation is in crisis and there's no one else who's following this trail. Who could gain volunteers who had pledged to uphold the Constitution and now seem determined to undermine the Presidency? Where do senators and the vice-president stand? Who can they trust? Nice yarn, well delivered.

For a change Scott Harveth is home, with his wife!!! This is no time for a rest though as Scott ans Solvi will have to stop coup, which can become an international incident. Much like today, some in the government do not like the new president, but unlike today they don't belittle him or use the courts or other methods to get thier message out. Instead they use guns, RPGs, serin gas and other lethal devices on people that are not the president for false flag events. As the new stay at home hubby goes to work, he already misses the field and does not disappoint. Biggest question now is what's next?

Somehow I missed #1-#23 of Brad Thor's Scot Harvath series. However, this #24 book can be read stand-alone. No doubt men will enjoy reading about Swashbuckling Scot Spy Guy with his gear, guns, and cars as he goes after the bad guys amidst the crazy politicians in Washington, DC. It all seemed to focus on urgent issues of national security. Scot wastes no time whatsoever after returning from his honeymoon with his new wife, Sølvi Kolstad, who is with Norwegian Intelligence. There were oodles of characters (30+) and lots of action as Scot protects the ex-Secretary of State so no doubt this book could easily be made into a movie.

The 24th book in the series. I read the last two back-to-back to catch up. See my review of Shadow of Doubt to get my feelings on this title character and the author. One of the things I like about this series is that the stories closely resemble current events and technology, the author stays closely aligned with our news cycle and world events. In Edge of Honor it is very similar to the current Trump administration, and America’s growing distrust in its own government and security administrations. Of course, the bad guys are tending to be Russians in all these latest novels. Hurray for the hero, Scot Horvath, again.

It might be because I have not read Thor in a bit but I actually enjoyed this book much more than the past few entries in the series. Scott is finally back on the states, and the plot for this book is much more simple and happens over a few days rather than months and spanning so many places. It was easy to keep up with and enjoy. At the same time I am read for Scott to retire. I think that we are getting to a point where the character just needs to be let go. It’s been enough. I’m ready for the series to end. And with the new book being published this year we will see what happens. 4/5 stars

If there was a Mount Rushmore for Thriller Authors Brad Thor would definitely be on it. In this story a Corrupt Senator and his Co-Conspirators try to remove the Current President and put the Vice President into power by recruiting Ex Military and Ex Secret Service Members by orcustrating attacks that would force the President to resign. My favorite part of the story was when Scot Harvath fought and defeated one of the Co-Conspirators Hale who was a giant but Harvath used his skills to take him down

Thor is one of my favorite authors and I’ve read all his books, yet this one was a disappointment. This felt like a book that was quickly written to make the NYT Best Seller list and collect a check. The plot was very thin, only loosely tied together in the end. There weren’t any intriguing characters like most of his other novels have. The suspense and the feeling of being taken along on an adventure ride, which Thor is known for, was absent. This is Thor’s worst book by far and I hope it’s not a sign of things to come. If you are a Scot Harvath fan (like me), it’s best to skip this one.

Edge of Honor By Brad Thor This was the first book I read by this author. It was a page-turner filled with twists and turns. The plot involved deception and conspiracy theories. The main character was drawn into a scheme that could threaten the American government. Taken from today’s headlines, the democracy of this government feels volatile. With the political climate being chaotic, you never know who to trust. Harvath has to make impossible decisions to prevent the government from being overthrown. The book was a good read.

Scot Harvath and his bride have spent six months traveling around the globe on their honeymoon only To return to an attack on the Norwegian Embassy. This throws them Into the midst of turmoil,deceit,and Political politics. The stakes are high and the CIA and FBI are involved In the conspiracy. There are Enemies all around and Scot and his people hope they can ring it all to a satisfying conclusion and Apprehend the right people. This is a well written book and series and has plenty of action and thrills. Recommended.

2.5 to 3 Stars I am in the middle of the road on this one . . . it has the typical feel of a John Grisham novel, and I thought at first it might come in highly for me. But, something odd happened about 2/3 of the way through it . . . The pros: - Unique and intriguing plot/mystery: A mysterious death during a hurricane? Yes, please! - Fun characters: I like all the people we meet on Camino Island. Most of them are quirky writer types with interesting backgrounds. The (maybe) cons: - Grisham and food: I have said in previous reviews that one of the biggest things I have always noticed with Grisham from the very first time I read him, he has to give detailed accounts of all the food and drinks consumed by his characters. This was very obvious in Camino Winds. I think the book would be about one fourth shorter if the food a drink mentions were removed. Maybe not really a con, but it just stands out as filler (and makes me hungry and thirsty) - The rush job: This was the odd part for me that kind of soured the whole experience. Grisham spent a couple hundred pages developing this intricate mystery and setting up all the situations and characters with a precarious heightened intensity. Then, I guess he got a call from his publisher saying the book was due because suddenly it was several weeks later and everything that had been built up was summarized in a few pages and it moved on to the end game of the novel. I felt a bit cheated to have everything I have been getting into resolved with some Clif Notes. This happened to me last year with another book (Gwendy’s Magic Feather) and I was much harsher on that one – mainly because I don’t think the rush job led to a bad ending like it did with that one. But, still . . . let me know if you read this one and felt the same way – it just stood out so much that it was shocking! I was speechless! I checked to see if some part of the copy I had was missing! A decent book if you like the Grisham formula. But, don’t be surprised if you are looking for the missing pages like I was.
2.5 stars! The plotline was both frustrating and a bit dull to get through plus parts were very questionable with this book #2...

Love a good Grisham novel! This is not a legal thriller, but a murder mystery set on Camino Island. It is the second book in this series but can absolutely be read as a stand alone. It is a fun, twisty read that I read in a weekend. Bruce Cable returns in this book after his adventure Camino Island. He is the owner of Bay Books, the indie bookstore that everybody wants to visit. The store is about to welcome back Mercer Mann, the writer with a connection to the Island. But Hurricane Leo has other ideas and is headed straight for them. Most people head for the mainland but Bruce stays to try to protect his store. In the aftermath of the storm. Bruce is told of the death of writer and friend Nelson Kerr. At first look it appears that it was the storm that killed him but the closer they look the more it appears to be murder. Local police get nowhere with the case so Bruce and his friends start investigating . Who would want Nelson dead and why? Could his unpublished manuscript hold the key? I really enjoyed this fast paced and thrilling story. Grisham fans will love it, even if it is not a legal thriller. His writing is brilliant and his characters full of life. Highly recommend. Thank you Hachette Australia for my copy of this book to read.

Disappointing. Not as disappointing as John Grisham’s last release, The Guardians, but still pretty disappointing because Camino Island is arguably my favorite Grisham novel. If you didn’t like that one, you’ll likely dig this one, and vice versa. Grisham stripped away almost everything I loved about that book—the languid pace, the light romance, the writer community characters—and instead focused his sights on writing a high-concept thriller that almost reminded me of mid-tier Dean Koontz in its the latter half. Still, this is John Grisham. He’s a seasoned veteran, so anything he publishes is at least readable. I gave this 3 stars after all; there were bits and pieces I liked. The first third or so I dug, it’s only when the few characters left over from Camino Island started investigating I lost interest. Dunno why. I felt like I was reading Stephen King’s Bill Hodges trilogy without the weird quirks and fast pace that made those books such a joy. This is Grisham without personality, without flavor. It’s his courtroom thriller thing without a courtroom or lawyer. It shows occasional flashes of the color and inspiration that made its predecessor such a success, but most of the time it’s a fairly standard investigative crime thriller, hold the thrilling. I came away from this feeling empty, not hating or loving it. Indifference.

John Grisham knocks this one out of the park SUMMARY Bookstore owner Bruce Cable’s is preparing for the return of bestselling author Mercer Mann to his store on Camino Island when a hurricane heads directly for the island. A mandatory evacuation is ordered, but Bruce decides to stay and ride out the category 4 storm. The Hurricane Leo devastates the island. Homes, hotels and storefronts were demolished and several people died. One of the victims is Nelson Kerr, an author and friend of Bruce’s, who is asked to identify the body. Nelson’s injuries look suspicious to Bruce. But who would want Nelson dead? The local police are overwhelmed with the storm and are ill equipped to handle a murder case right now so Cable takes matter into his own hands. Could Nelson’s murder be related a book he is working on? Was someone trying to keep him quiet? REVIEW John Grisham knocks it out of the park once again. CAMINO WINDS is a perfect read. The writing is seamless, the characters are intriguing and the story is riveting. You will be hooked from page one. Grisham’s description of Hurricane Leo brought back memories for me of Hurricane Michael from 2018. While the path wasn’t quite the same, I can still hear the cracking and crashing trees and branches and the howling winds much like described in the book. Even the impassable roads and the indescribable devastation of the homes and businesses in the aftermath was similar. Unfortunately a year and a half later, much of the devastation that occurred during Hurricane Michael still exists to this day in many parts of Northwest Florida. Based on his descriptions I have to think that Grisham has survived one or more hurricanes. My favorite part was Bruce Cable’s intriguing character and the repartee he had with his friends. I appreciated the effort Bruce’s and his friends took to ensure that the cops treated Nelson’s death as a murder and not just as a result of the Hurricane. Publisher Doubleday Books Published April 28, 2020 Narrated Michael Beck Review www.bluestockingreviews.com

Typical Grisham…which I always enjoy! I like the familiarity of his novels. The characters and setting of the Camino series are likable and interesting! Looking forward to reading the third of this series!
Probably closer to 2.5. Not as enjoyable as Camino Island. Not sure now if I want to read the third book

Mr Grisham...can we have a chat? Just between you and me sir...who ACTUALLY wrote this book? Was this a first draft that got sent to the printer on accident and it was like "welp, we printed them, too late now"? If it weren't for all the food references (typical Grisham writing), I would think you let an assistant write this book sir. I felt like I was reading a Nancy Drew book...super outdated writing and unrealistic character actions/reactions. The heart of the story was fantastic. But the execution of it was underwhelming. This is definitely the worst John Grisham book I've read out of the 12-15 I've read. Luckily for readers, it appears each book can act as a stand alone in this trilogy. Camino Island was fantastic! But this one, if you aren't a John Grisham fan and must read everything he writes, I wouldn't recommend this one. I am still going to move on to the last book in the trilogy next. Fingers crossed we finish strong!

So..Grisham is one of the authors I always read. I loved the first Camino island book. And while I didn’t hate this one...it wasn’t nearly as good. This is not quite 3...not as bad as 2 stars! Why won’t goodreads give us half stars?

3.5 ⭐️s Camino Island was my first Grisham read ever, and boy did I walk away loving that one. It was a quirky mix of thriller, light romance, and action-tinged crime caper. It was an oddly captivating gem. Very little of that came through in this second novel. This felt much more sterile, awkwardly paced and boiler plate to me. It was starved of the wildly beguiling dynamic between Bruce and Mercer, and the fact that Mercer played such an insignificant role in this book drove me crazy. All that said, I still breezed through this one in a day, and never once felt bored. Why You Should Or Shouldn’t Read It You should. It’s still a nice Sunday morning read when you want to escape the doldrums, stresses and constant need for the pesky need for elevated thought Themes Nothing lofty here. Just a good ol’ fashioned thriller without much thematic richness. One Thing I’ll walk away with A strong hope that Mercer makes a triumphant return in the next book

“If you ask me, there’s nothing more boring than a sober writer.” This text is not good. I enjoyed its predecessor, CAMINO ISLAND, for what it was. A fun white-collar caper. But CAMINO WINDS is just dumb! First off, there are so many details about so many things that have nothing to do with anything. Most of these details in no manner advance the story. Another irritation is that the book’s protagonist, bookstore owner Bruce Cable, who I found somewhat charming in the first book to feature him is an absolute dud in this one. Plus, he ALWAYS seems to have a drink in his hand. Always! Should someone tell Mr. Grisham that his protagonist has a problem? Final summation, it’s just a terrible book. Poorly plotted, poorly written, poorly executed.

Always enjoy Grisham who either knocks it out of the park with his legal thrillers or writes a good solid legal thriller. Have to admit that I haven't read any of his "side subject books" for example his books on baseball. Tried Calico Joe but put it down for later as I love watching my home team Astros but I do not enjoy reading anything about sports. Back to Camino Island... I adore books with characters that are campy and this book as well as Camino Winds has those in spades. Besides engaging storylines the character development in these first two books was strong. I of course own a copy of Camino Ghosts but haven't read it yet as I am so far behind on my physical TBR. Then their is book club and my Goodreads discussion groups which I quite enjoy.

The most exciting aspect of this read is a hurricane named Leo and a student named Nick! A ‘cozy’ style mystery that gets no-where fast. It is trying so hard to be quirky it misses on all fronts. If it did not have Grisham’s name on the cover I’m pretty sure the ratings would be lower. I enjoyed ‘Camino Island, but can’t with any honesty recommend Book #2.
Back to Camino Island and the gang! First book is much better.

Not one of Grisham’s best work, but overall, not bad. I thought the story in Camino Island was better & its plots were more fun to read… The first half of this novel was really slow reading. However, the second half really picks up the pace. The ending of this book felt like a let down & was disappointing… Hopefully, the third book of the series, Camino Ghost, will be better.

This novel is a true page-turner, driven by a compelling plot and a memorable cast of characters. From the very beginning, the story moves at a brisk pace, making it difficult to put down—I finished it quickly because I was so eager to see what would happen next. The characters are well-developed, each with distinct quirks that add depth and make them genuinely likable. Overall, it’s another strong book from Grisham and one I would highly recommend to fans of fast-paced, character-driven fiction.

For my detailed review of this book please visit - https://rb.gy/kwm4yq This happens to be a rather average book from John Grisham, though only when compared to his legal thrillers. As a standalone novel, this is good enough..
Not bad, but not up to Grisham's standard

This, the author's second adventure set on Camino Island, puts some of the characters from the first (appropriately titled Camino Island) back in the eye of the storm. This time, though, it's literally; not long after the story begins, Hurricane Leo threatens to disrupt the festivities honoring successful author Mercer Mann that are to take place in Bruce Cable's Bay Books store. Mercer, who has a college teaching gig, has returned to the island with her latest boy toy, Thomas, expecting to be wined and dined by her old friends. But it's not long before all those plans are blowin' in the wind; Leo, it seems, has set his eye on the island's downtown. Evacuations are ordered, but Bruce and a couple of his friends decide to ride it out. Luckily, they survive the devastation; but no such luck for Nelson Kerr, a thriller writer and one of Bruce's friends. He's found dead at his damaged home; but an up-close-and-personal look determines that Leo may not have been the killer. Since Nelson died in the storm when debris was flying everywhere, the local police aren't quite ready to buy the murder angle - and even if they did, they're up to their eyeballs in clean-up efforts and making sure looters don't start running rampant. Bruce, though, is positive he's right. As he and his friends, including Mercer and Thomas, put their heads together, the consensus is that somebody, somewhere, didn't want Nelson's not-yet-published manuscript to see the light of print. But who might that be? Surely not one of their own - each of whom has a background and secrets that are slowly revealed as the story unfolds - and issues are resolved - over a period of a year or so. As was the first book, it's told in a narrative style, although there seems to be more dialogue here (and, maybe because of that, I think I slightly prefer this one). Those expecting courtroom theatrics will be disappointed, although lawyers do get involved in some of the goings-on. All in all, this one is thoroughly enjoyable - and I've definitely taken a liking to this series. More, please!

The continuing adventures of Bay Books, it's owner Bruce this time taking centre stage, and the writer community on Camino Island. Points to Grisham for finding a plot that allows him to bring back all of the characters from the first book, and giving them a new story. The action veers somewhat unrealistically into pharma-conspiracy and hitmen and the interest drops a bit once we leave the island, and the central characters, behind in the 2nd half of the novel, but overall a satisfactory sequel.

The first third of the book sets the scene nicely on Camino Island, however it shifts away from this for the remainder and drifts along without being overly gripping. Waited for drama throughout but it never appeared. Disappointed for my first venture into the John Grisham universe.

This book took me awhile to read but not because of the book but the fact that I was moving and renovating while reading it. I enjoyed this book a lot and loved the way the story unraveled. The characters were well developed and the plot moved at a constant pace. Another great book by John Grisham! Highly recommend.
